### Established facts

1. **SEVERANCE 6, taken at ch 588 on day 1,772, the nineteenth of the month beginning 1,754** — the pinned 75-day
   interval from Severance 5 at day 1,697 (1,772 − 1,697 = 75). Taken at the second hour of the nineteenth, at a bar on
   two posts four hundred yards east of the turn, with a carter of thirty-five thirty feet off on a box and the bar on the
   board bare. **Bracket 3 of Volume 10's three in sixty-two**, in the far-side house form, on its own line. **No figure of
   what is left of him is stated.**
2. **The sixth cost, named once, on the page, in her own mouth, at ch 588: SHE CANNOT KEEP WHAT SHE FINDS BY HOLDING IT.**
   Finding stops being keeping; holding is somebody else's work. **It is shown working three times:** her own heelprint
   ninety seconds old and un-findable standing on the spot · a room behind a window that will not stay a room · **nine
   coppers counted four times on a store counter, four answers.** A finding holds about two hours in her, and the only
   way to keep one is to walk it while she has it. **It is the engine of the batch and Volume 11 inherits it whole.**
3. **The lever — asking twice.** Written in the dust at the fourth foot of an opening at ch 594 on the eighteenth of the
   month beginning 1,784 and **rubbed out and not written again**, after a hundred and forty-eight days of carrying it.
   **Not pulled anywhere in this batch.** `I would not have stopped you.` — *I know that.*
4. **The last asking, ch 595, day 1,802, the seventh hour.** One at a time, at the wall, in daylight, with the boy of
   fifteen four feet off behind her and a carter two miles west of the gate. She asks **what else is on it**, standing
   since day 1,627, one hundred and seventy-six days. **He answers the smallest thing on the page and the answer is not a
   name: a number. Six.** She had counted **four** go over the chain at the fourth hour of the twelfth of the month
   beginning 1,784 and had thought the number was four. **Three questions stand and there is no fifth and no book left to
   put them into.**
5. **THE IRREVERSIBLE STEPS, both of them, in the outline's order.** **ch 596 — he shuts the book** on a plank table in
   daylight with nothing on it, in four seconds, and neither of them asks the other for anything, and it cannot be
   un-shut. **ch 598 — she finds Ning Wu alive, in person, in her hearing, once**, and it cannot be un-found.
6. **Shuyin.** Shuts the book at the ninth hour of the closing day, walks thirteen miles west to the turn with her in
   five days, says *you do not have a road, go east*, goes east. **Alive, old, correct, not thanked, and he returns.**
   **The wall stays open behind him and nobody shut it.** `Shuyin` **0** by name across fourteen chapters, `Warden` **0**,
   matching Batch 0003's measurement and the volume's pattern.
7. **Him.** `Yuan` **0** by name across fourteen chapters. **On the page once, at ch 596**, in one sentence, in the
   present tense: *He is not going to stop it and I did not ask him to.* **No figure of what is left of him is stated
   before or after.** He opens no wall and is wrong-sided from day 1,521. **He is not thanked.**
8. **Ning Wu, in person, once.** **Alive, nineteen, nine years in a barrow ground beyond the opening, at the first hour
   of the first of the month beginning 1,814 (day 1,814).** First words: *you are shorter.* **He does not forgive her and
   has not: *you can come, it is not the same as being let.*** He does not know what a list is and does not know what
   *lost* means. `Ning Wu` is **1** on the page in these fourteen chapters, said out loud once, in her own mouth.
9. **New geography this batch, described once and not to be re-derived.** **The chain:** a burn in a cut nine feet deep
   with three planks and a chain at the near end, where the strip road ends and the made road begins, kept by an unnamed
   man of fifty-five who took it over because **the man who had it before is alive and does not come back.** It is opened
   in daylight for anybody who asks and is not opened at night. **The ground beyond the opening:** a made road running
   east, rows of barrows cut and filled with a stone at the head of each, about two hundred people, no man over any of
   them, nobody paid, no board and no chalk and no rate said out loud, and not one person in nine years has come back out
   of it.
10. **The wheel-marks.** Found at ch 588 in the dew east of the bar on two posts, nine years healed, running east-northeast
    about eleven miles and coming out on the gate road a quarter of a mile beyond the opening. **Gone by the twenty-seventh
    and not findable again.** It is the batch's engine and **it is the road that was never told her.**
11. **Wei Ran — Volume 10's second and last card to her, at ch 589.** Carried twice at a rate of six coppers the four
    miles, **the number said out loud both times**, one opinion, one sentence about a bar not going on the seat. **No
    gift, nothing a romance, no coppers chased.**
12. **Structural mouths four and five of the volume, both inside the three-to-seven range.** **ch 593, an unnamed man of
    fifty-five who keeps the crossing chain: five short sentences** — not a place to join, not a punishment, kept things
    go where kept things go, the going is exact, and he has not said it since a man with a bar asked him once. **ch 594,
    the same man, on why he said it to her: four short sentences.** The volume's five mouths are 544, 561, 577, 581 and
    593 and all five are on the page.
13. **Untouched and unraised, each a fact and not a topic.** The paper against her ribs, opened and never named, and
    **there are two things against her ribs and she has called neither of them anything** · the plate still worn and
    undescribed · the register still *reconciled* · *kiln-born* in two heads on no paper · what became of the eleven not
    raised · the four months never named · the ch 150 refusal never softened · no page of his book read out loud and no
    name ever read · **the year of non-forgiveness not mentioned once in fourteen chapters** · no harem and nothing a
    romance · **she never says her mother's name** · the relicensing legs never named.
14. **She never thanks him and never thanks Shuyin.** The only thank you in the batch is not said at all; she decides at
    ch 600 that she is not going to say one to either of them, and **no card writes a scene in which she does.** She has
    not thanked a man of nine hundred years in nine years except for four sentences in the month beginning 1,694 that she
    did not expect to buy anything. She has not thanked her brother either.
15. **The eight leaves.** **Put down once at ch 538 and moved once at ch 563 by her own two hands. The flat stone under
    the bottom of the ladder is bare and nothing in this batch puts anything on it. The six blank leaves stay blank:**
    she took the book out at ch 600 on the fourteenth of the month beginning 1,814, held it for an hour with a nib and a
    cake of ink she has not used in two months, and put it back.
16. **The voice, named once at ch 600 and not explained.** Something in her head has counted with her for eight years and
    has never once said what it was before it started counting. **She does not ask him yet. He is still talking.**
    **That is the last line of Volume 10.**
17. ***Twenty-two days* is STILL OPEN** and was put in front of her again at ch 590, out loud, and **was not equated to
    any dated interval.**
18. **The window a hundred yards off the east side, and the lime under the bar of the shut door.** The window is STILL
    OPEN: she went through the opening for the first time at ch 591, stood under the sill for two hours, **spent none of
    its four questions**, and could not hold what she saw. **The lime is LEFT, unspent, and was not turned into anything.**

### The walk of `outline/volume-10.md`, section by section, with a verdict on each item

#### 1. The volume goal — **NOT HELD IN ITS LITERAL FORM, and this is reported and not softened and not repaired**

`outline/series.md` §9 fixes the goal as: *Ning Yan must find her brother before the Warden's list closes for good, or
Ning Wu stays a name on a page for another decade.*

**The page does not do that.** She asks the last question at the seventh hour of day 1,802 (ch 595). The book is shut at
the ninth hour of day 1,802 (ch 596). **She finds Ning Wu alive, in person, in her hearing, once, at the first hour of
the first of the month beginning 1,814 — day 1,814, which is twelve days after the closing.** The brother is found
**after** the list closed for good, not before it.

**The page says so itself, twice.** ch 599: *"On the nineteenth of a month beginning 1,784 he shut it in daylight with
nothing on the table and no one asked him to."* ch 600, *Two People She Has Not Thanked*: *"He is alive and old and not
thanked."* And the finding settles nothing: *"You can come. It is not the same as being let."*

**This is not a defect and the close does not call it one.** `outline/volume-10.md` §*Volume climax* item 3 fixes it in
terms: *Ch 598–599. The finding… **It settles nothing.*** And §*Fixed* fixes what "appear" costs: *in person, alive, in
her hearing, once, in Batch 0004, **and it settles nothing**.* **The volume is internally consistent, and the goal
sentence in `series.md` §9 and the volume's actual resolution are not the same sentence.** Recorded here with the page
quoted, exactly as the close was instructed. **Neither file may be edited by this phase and neither was.**

**Two related findings, and one state-file error:**

#### 6. The frame scene — **HELD, with one exception recorded**

**ch 584 is the only marked present-frame scene in the volume.** A scan of every line opening `He ` + a present-tense
verb across all sixty-two files returns present-tense narration about Yuan **only in ch 584**; every other hit is a
different man — the boy of eleven, the keeper, the man at the chain, Shuyin, Ning Wu. **No other character is ever in a
marked present frame.** ch 584 is the sixth after ch 272, 338, 401, 458 and 518, and it is the first of the six that is
about a list rather than about being found, sent for, asked, spent or opened.

**Yuan is on the page once in sixty-two chapters, at ch 596, in one sentence:**

> *"He is not going to stop it and I did not ask him to."*

**EXCEPTION RECORDED, NOT REPAIRED.** `outline/volume-10.md` says *every sentence Yuan speaks is written in the present
tense*. The lead clause is present; **the trailing clause `I did not ask him to` is past.** It is one clause in one
sentence in one chapter, it is a deliberate split between what is going to happen and a completed act, and Batch 0004's
review passed it. **Recorded so the register rule is not reported as cleanly held when it is not.**

**`Yuan` by name: 0 across the volume.** No figure of what is left of him is stated anywhere, before or after either
irreversible step. He opens no wall and is wrong-sided from day 1,521.

#### 7. The two irreversible steps, in order — **HELD, and neither is un-done anywhere**

**ch 596 — the shutting.** He shuts the book on a plank table in daylight at the ninth hour of the closing day with
nothing on it, in about four seconds, his hands staying on the cover for a count of thirty. **Neither of them asks the
other for anything.** No page read, no name read, nothing shown of what shutting does, and nothing on that ground
changed while it happened.

**ch 598 — the finding.** She finds Ning Wu alive, in person, in her hearing, once, at the first hour of the first of
the month beginning 1,814. Nineteen years old, nine years in a barrow ground beyond the opening, hands like her
father's, not surprised and not glad. First words: *you are shorter.* **You can come. It is not the same as being let.**

**Neither is undone.** ch 599 has her go back over it a hundred times and get nothing she can put anywhere; ch 600 has
the book still shut, his door shut, the six gone where kept things go, and a brother who will not walk with her. **The
book is never reopened, the finding is never withdrawn, and no later chapter offers a way round either.**

#### 8. The volume climax, ch 595–600 — **HELD, and the closing day is named once**

**The last asking (ch 595) · the shutting (ch 596–597) · the finding (ch 598–599) · the voice (ch 600).** All four
land in the outline's order and each is a complete scene.

**Day 1,802, the nineteenth of the month beginning 1,784, is named in daylight by him at ch 569–570** and is not
extended, renamed or moved. It appears thereafter as a fixed date she counts to, and in the last six chapters it is used
and never re-derived: ch 595 (she asks at the seventh hour of it), ch 596 (he shuts at the ninth hour of it), ch 598
(*"he shut the book on the nineteenth"*), ch 599, ch 600. **No last-page chapter moves it, extends it or gives it
another name.**

**One re-derivation, recorded: ch 571**, one chapter after the naming — *"Day one thousand eight hundred and two is the
nineteenth of the month beginning 1,784. She is standing on day one thousand six hundred and ninety-seven. One hundred
and five."* It is her own count in the dust and **1,802 − 1,697 = 105 is exact.** The month-rule derivation itself
happens once, at ch 570: *"The first of the month beginning 1,784 is day 1,784. The nineteenth is eighteen days on from
the first. Day 1,802."* **Recorded rather than smoothed.**

#### 14. The geography and the road — **THE SPINE HOLDS. SIX CONTRADICTIONS FOUND AND REPAIRED. ONE RECORDED AND NOT.**

**The settled spine, and the count on it, measured on the files as they now stand:**

> **post → 9 miles of strip road → turn → 11 miles of made road → gate → 2 miles → wall → opening. Total, twenty-two miles.**

**The nine-mile strip leg is stated 29 times and the eleven-mile made leg 24 times, across 29 of the sixty-two chapters,
and not one of the fifty-three contradicts the other.** *(The close published *seventeen and eleven times respectively
and never varied* and did not name the command that produced either number. **The close review could not reproduce that
pair under any reading and has replaced it with a count and a method:** every body-prose paragraph of all sixty-two files,
`\bnine\b(\s+\w+){0,2}\s+of\s+(the\s+)?strip` and the same pattern with *eleven* and *made*, case-insensitive, counted
within a paragraph and not across the paragraph break. **The spine is the same one. Only the claim about how often it is
said was unverifiable, and it is now a number with its command in the sentence with it.**)*

The bar on two posts is **four hundred yards east of the turn**, stated in ch 561, 588, 597, 599 and 600. The wheel-marks
**start at the bar and come out a quarter of a mile beyond the opening** (ch 588). The turn is **thirteen miles** west of
the wall (ch 591, 597, 600).

**Batch 0004's new ground — the chain, the ground beyond the opening, the barrow field, the wheel-marks — was checked
against every earlier statement and adds no contradiction of its own once the six below are repaired.** **There is
nothing between the gate and the wall to lie down on, and it is stated thirteen times across the volume, and in every
one of them the two-mile stretch is empty. No chapter puts anything there.** ✓

**Six statements contradicted the spine. Each was one figure, each is locally provable, and each is repaired:**

| Ch | Was | Now | The derivation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 541 | *"nine miles of strip road between this post and a turn, and **eleven** miles of made road between that turn and the wall"* | **the close changed this to *thirteen* and the close review put it back to *eleven*, adding *the last two miles of flat ground*** | **The original error was real — 9 + 11 read as 20 against a paragraph that says twenty-two — and the close's cure made it worse, because *thirteen miles of made road* contradicts seven chapters that give eleven to the made road and turns the turn-to-wall leg into made road when the spine puts two miles of it in flat ground. The page now reads *eleven miles of made road between that turn and the wall, and a gate on the made road with a boy of fifteen on a chain, and then the last two miles of flat ground and the opening in the wall*, which is 9 + 11 + 2 = 22 and is ch 558's own formulation** |
| 554 | *"At the wall means **eleven** miles of strip road and eleven of made road"* | **"nine miles of strip road and eleven of made road and two of the last of it"** | the volume's own canonical formulation, at ch 558, word for word |
| 582 | *"eleven miles of strip and **nine** of made and two past a gate"* | **"nine of strip and eleven of made and two past a gate"** | ch 574 has the identical sentence with the two legs the right way round |
| 592 | *"there were **nine** miles of made road and a gate and a wall"* | **eleven** | eleven is stated ten times; nine was never a made-road figure |
| 595 | *"walked **nine** miles of made road with the gate at the ninth hour"* | **eleven** | same |
| 597 | *"a line in wet ground east of a bar on two posts, **eleven** miles across open country"* | **thirteen** | a quarter of a mile to the turn + 11 to the gate + 2 to the wall + a quarter past the opening. Eleven was two and a half short |

**The 541 row is the one the close review reversed, and the reversal is recorded here rather than quietly applied: the
spine above is stated twenty-four times to the made leg and the page now says eleven everywhere, without a contradiction.
`thirteen` remains the figure for the turn's distance from the wall and for the walk east of a bar, and those are two
different measurements.**

**ONE FINDING RECORDED AND NOT REPAIRED — the lane.** ch 560 says, in three consecutive sentences:

> *"The lane is four miles west of the turn. The turn is nine miles east of the post. The lane is thirteen miles from the
> post."*

**Nine minus four is five, not thirteen, and the three sentences cannot all be true.** ch 560 then builds fourteen miles
out and back, twenty-eight for the days and forty-four for a question on the thirteen. Meanwhile ch 585 and ch 600 both
list, unprompted, *"A cottage four miles west. A mill five miles west. **A lane four miles west** with a woman at forty
feet of it."* **Two incompatible canons are on the page and this close did not choose between them.** Correcting
*thirteen* to *five* would break three sums inside ch 560; correcting *four miles west of the turn* would contradict
ch 585 and ch 600 and the road-running line at ch 574. **Recorded with both sides quoted and not repaired.**

heaviest chapters are **586, 596 and 600 at 13 each**, then 593 and 598 at 12.

**No cap was set for it, so the volume does not fail a gate on this, and this close cut no instance** — every `nothing`
in those five chapters is load-bearing (`nothing on the plank table` is the image ch 596 is built on; `nothing sweeps a
flat at the west jamb` is a concrete fact about a wall; `there is nothing on the board` is ch 600's title beat). **It is
handed to Volume 11's first batch as an open craft line, not as a continuity thread.**

#### The deliberate repetitions, counted and named

**24 cross-chapter paragraph repeats, all deliberate, none a duplicated paragraph in the sense the budget means:**

- **The three terms, said seven times and never re-explained:** *"One at a time. At the wall. In daylight."* (ch 554, 583,
  594, 595) and *"'One at a time,' he said. 'At the wall. In daylight.'"* (ch 554, 558, 565).
- **The first question, twice:** *"What else is on it," Ning Yan said* (ch 546, 553) and *"Will you walk the last two
  miles with me," Ning Yan said* (ch 553, 570).
- **The name, twice and both times out loud:** *"Ning Wu."* (ch 585 to the man of nine hundred years, ch 598 to her
  brother). **This is the volume's spine.**
- **The lever, twice:** *"Asking twice."* (ch 582, ch 594). **The not-writing, twice:** *"He did not write."* (ch 580,
  585). **The brother's answer, twice:** *"Ning Wu, she said."* (ch 568, 572).
- **Counting beats:** *"Yes."* ×3 · *"No."* ×6 · *"Six."* ×2 · *"Nine."* ×2 · *"All right," Ning Yan said.* ×3.

**6 within-chapter repeats, all deliberate and all the volume's arithmetic:** ch 543 *"I have none," Ning Yan said.* ×2 ·
ch 556 *"Nine."* ×2 · ch 577 *"'Yes.'"* ×2 · ch 588 *"She could not find it."* ×2 · ch 592 *"Nine."* ×3 · ch 593
*"Four."* ×2 · ch 595 *"'Six.'"* ×2 and *"Six."* ×2. **Cutting any of them would cut the counting, which is the only
instrument the protagonist owns.**

#### Two records on the zeros that did not come out at zero

1. **`the walls` is 1, at ch 591, on a homonym** — the walls of a room behind a window. Full quotation and reasoning in
   item 11 above. **Recorded as 1. Not repaired.**
2. **`reader` is 3 and the widened scaffolding pattern is 0.** All three are the plain English noun — *"no reader on nine
   days of road could be sent for"* (ch 544) · *"a book… that has a reader in it now that she did not put there"* (ch
   544) · *"she is not going to pretend to him or to a reader that the flatness hurt"* (ch 577). **None is the
   authorial sense. The widened pattern is 0 and the bare form is 3, and both are published rather than one.**

**And the one that is a genuine hit: `N volumes` returns 1.** ch 600, in the last thematic paragraph of the volume:

> *"Ten volumes of roads and four walls and a furnace that will not light itself and a hand that cannot write a false
> line, and she has never asked it what it was."*

**This close records it at 1 against an allowance of 0, and does not repair it.** It is a measure-word use — ten great
cartloads of road — sitting in a list whose other three items are four walls, a furnace and a hand, all of them in-world
objects. **Rewriting the volume's closing paragraph to satisfy a grep would be exactly the softening repair this close
was forbidden to make, and a reader cannot take it for a meta-joke when *four walls* is in the same breath.** It is
recorded here so that the allowance is not reported as cleanly held when it is not.

### What Volume 11 inherits, in one page

**DAY 1,830, the seventeenth of the month beginning 1,814, at ch 600.** She is standing at the turn on the store road at
dusk with a bar on her shoulder, a bag, and a brother nine miles further east walking west.

**Severance 6**, six stages past the ceiling, **nineteen years old**. Four fingers and a thumb on the right hand · the
right arm open four days in five · eight of eleven holds · four counts of breath, seven on a rise · a small open place
low behind her fourth rib, the size of a coin, open since the eighteenth of the month beginning 1,544, and the merit has
not come out of it since ch 588. **Being lighter every single day since the eighteenth of the month beginning
1,544 — that eighteenth is day 1,561, the count is inclusive of the first day, and the figure at any day D is
D − 1,560, which is 270 days of it at day 1,830. Not hungry.**

**She has lost, in the order the volume took it:** being counted where she stands · following where she is told ·
keeping what she finds by holding it. **Three questions stand in a shut book and there is no fourth and no book in the
world she is permitted to put a question into.**

**Still open and still to be open:** the voice, which has counted with her for eight years and has never once said what
it was before it started counting · what *lost* does · the Hunter's request, pending, and he is not on the page and
never named · the window a hundred yards off the east side, open, four questions unspent · the lime under the bar of the
shut door, unspent · *twenty-two days*, open and equated to nothing · the lever, asking twice, rubbed out and not written
again · the eleven, the four months, the register *reconciled*, the plate, *kiln-born*, a hut's light she does not know
went out · six people gone where kept things go, four of them counted at a chain and two never seen · **the walls,
which stay** · and the year, which is still carrying and is not mentioned once.

**The doors are shut:** the book, his door, the list. **The roads:** post to turn 9 · turn to gate 11 · gate to wall 2 ·
beyond the opening, a made road east into a barrow ground of about two hundred people that nobody comes back out of.

**And the question the volume ends on is the one it did not ask:** not what he will tell her, and not whether she will
forgive anybody, and not what is on a list that is shut. **She does not ask him yet. He is still talking.**

### The things this batch resolved, closed, or paid

1. **THE ASKING, DONE AND IRREVERSIBLE.** ch 609, the ninth hour of the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 1,814,
   day 1,837, alone, on broken ground a hundred yards north of a turn, after she has checked there is not a soul within
   four hundred yards. **It cannot be un-asked and the second person who holds the words is him.**
2. **THE TERMS, NAMED AND NOT MOVED FOR THE REST OF THE VOLUME: one at a time · in daylight.** **The old third term,
   *at the wall*, is dead, because the wall is gone — and that is what makes the new third term *standing* and not a
   distance.** `outline/volume-11.md` fixes the terms and Batch 0001 named them on the page exactly once.
3. **THE COUNT MISSES ON MONEY, AND THE REASON IS NOT DIFFICULTY.** Nine coppers, nineteen stones, two hundred and
   eighty days, six leaves, eleven barrows: the instrument works on everything except the thing that moves. **This is the
   sixth cost applied and never re-derived.**
4. **THE TWENTY-TWO IS STILL OPEN AND STILL UNPLACED.** It comes back once, at ch 603, on a flat on the far side of a
   wall: **twenty-two, with no unit on it**, held for ninety seconds, gone when she stands, not returned on eleven miles
   and not returned since. **It is equated to no dated interval and nothing in this batch explains it.**
5. **THE FIRST ORIGIN MOUTH IS ON THE PAGE AND IS WITHIN ITS RANGE.** Six sentences, five speeches, none of them a
   speech. **The tenth part is not given and nothing proves the crews wrong** — he is flatly correct that not one man at
   that fire was cruel and that both of those are how it happened. **He does not know the name and he will not guess
   one: *He had a name and nobody at that fire used it*, and she does not ask again.**
6. **THE BROTHER IS WALKED PAST ONCE AND LET GO, AND THE LETTING COSTS THE WALKING.** ch 605, the store road, the eighth
   hour of the twenty-second, going west with a mill-sack. She stood at a shut door a mile short of him the day before
   **because going to the mill would be following him**, and this is what that decision is worth.
7. **MERIT SETTLES ONCE IN THIS BATCH**, at ch 611, on listed work cleared past the line at a stone face, not on a
   death. Eleven seconds, no sound in it because there is no one inside to be told, the sound goes into the ground, and
   **what it took came out of the ground under her feet and not out of her hands.** **No figure of what is left of him is
   stated anywhere in the batch.**
8. **THE BENCH LOOKS BACK.** ch 612. The woman of sixty turns her head about a foot and looks at the place low behind
   her fourth rib through the front of the coat, four seconds, and says nothing. **Nine years back from the twenty-seventh
   of the month beginning 1,814 is the eighteenth of the month beginning 1,544, and the lime, the wheel, the boy of ten
   behind the last barrow and the aperture are all on that one date.**
9. **THE SIX BLANK LEAVES ARE STILL BLANK AND NOTHING IN THE BATCH PUTS A NIB NEAR THEM.** ch 613 takes them out and
   counts them five times and gets six five times and writes nothing on any of them. **Batch 0002 inherits six blank
   leaves and ch 624 spends one.**
10. **THE LEVER IS CARRIED AND DECLINED TWICE AND IS NOT PULLED** — at ch 609 in the dark and at ch 614 in the open.
    **The reason is on the page: a thing you can ask twice is a thing you can be refused twice, and she wants a thing
    she can ask once.**
11. **THE SMALLEST TRUE THING.** ch 615. **A furnace, a number, nineteen: *Bricks. Two hundred and forty courses in a day
    at six hundred and forty to a course. I was the one who counted them. I have been counting bricks since I was eleven
    years old and I have never once been paid for it.*** **He gives three things where she asked for one, and the
    chapter says why: he hands over entries and not sentences, and he has done it since she was eight.** She takes no
    fourth thing. **One at a time.**

### What Batch 0002 inherits, unchanged

Severance 6 and the ninth stage landing at ch 616 on day 1,842 with **the volume's first bracketed layer line and
nothing else in fifteen chapters of Batch 0002 either outside ch 616.** The asking stands. The terms stand. The lever
stands, carried and un-pulled. **One copper, a quarter of a loaf, a bar nine feet nine, a bag with seven things in it, a
paper against her ribs never named, and six blank leaves.** A furnace east of here, not this sect. **Twenty-two** with
no unit on it. The window unasked, the lime left with her hand four inches off the bar, the hut light standing. One
elementary count of the days of going lighter, derivable only from the day. **Nothing forgiven, nothing thanked, no
mother's name said, no romance, and a brother nine miles east who will not walk with her.**

### THE SIX SENTENCES, defined

Given at the turn on the twenty-fourth by a man of forty-five who wanted nothing: the boy weighed them before they went
in · nobody pays him, his father fires · a boy who counts what nobody is paying him to count is a boy the furnace will
use · it is not the same thing as keeping and not one man at a fire thinks it is, and the only people who ever found
the difference out were the ones it was done to · it happened without anybody meaning it and not one man there was
cruel · he had a name and nobody at that fire used it. **Ch 608 counts them on the page; ch 609, ch 610, ch 613 and
ch 614 quote the artifact. They are spent. A chapter that puts him in a room again must not re-offer them as new.**

### The question she has carried, dated

Since the **fifteenth of the month beginning 1,634** — the question that got no answer back, and the moment ch 606
reconstructs. It was not *the month beginning 1,574* and it was never eight years. Asked out loud at ch 609 on day
1,837. It cannot be un-asked.

### The things this batch resolved, closed, or paid

1. **THE SEVENTH STAGE AND ITS COST, NAMED ONCE.** She cannot hear what she is told about him, **and the chapter is
   about the telling missing** — at ch 617 with a name out of a stranger's mouth, at ch 626 with ninety-one courses,
   and at ch 627 with a date read aloud out of her own book.
2. **THE COST RUNS BOTH WAYS AND THE CHAPTER SAYS IT.** A page she read with her own eyes held for a name and did not
   hold for a morning. **She was not in it.** That is the finding and it is not softened at ch 630.
3. **`Yuan Sheng`, TOLD AND THEN WRITTEN.** Told at ch 617 by a woman who had not said it in nineteen years, and it
   did not arrive. **Written at ch 624, in her own hand, on the third leaf of a book of eight, with the date from the
   page above it and *furnace ground* above that — and it cannot be put back un-written.**
4. **THE SIX SENTENCES OF CH 622.** They wrote it down the same week and they wrote it down true · my husband did not
   write the order and did not carry it out · the boy was nineteen and was the son of the man who keeps the fire · it
   did not save my husband and it did not save the boy · not one person on that ground has ever said it was going to.
   **The tenth part is not given and nothing proves the crews wrong.**
5. **THE HARVEST NAMED AT CH 630**, by her own reading, and **he says the one sentence that has never been said: the
   fire did not take all of it, and the part that woke up is the part that survived.** **He also says why he never
   said it: a question in the dark gets a shape and this does not go in the air, it goes into a book and cannot come
   out of it, and he did not want a page in the world with this on it that she had to carry.**
6. **THE BILL IS HERS AND IT IS COUNTABLE.** The second barrow, the bowl, four days of silence. **Her own asking at
   ch 609 put the knowing into the world twenty-six days before the cruel sentence on the step, and the ground has
   been closing on her since, and she is the only person alive who can say she did not expect it.** *(The review found
   this at thirty-three; the asking is the twenty-eighth of the month beginning 1,814, day 1,841, and the step is the
   twenty-fourth of the month beginning 1,844, day 1,867.)*
7. **SHE FORFEITED A BOARD** by leaving the turn on the twenty-ninth, and she said out loud that she was going
   anyway and that there would be two of them holding it.
8. **SHE SAID THE CRUELEST SENTENCE OF HER LIFE** at ch 621 and it did not turn out to be cruelty: **the woman opened
   the book on the thirtieth of the month beginning 1,844 at the sixth hour, having been up since the third.**
9. **THE RATE, AND THE COPPER THAT WILL NOT COUNT.** A fifth of a man's rate and the same board, four days a week off,
   eight coppers on a table in a cloth on the second of the month beginning 1,904, **nine in the bag, counted four
   times and never once nine.**
10. **THE LEVER IS CARRIED AND NOT PULLED** anywhere in this batch. **The terms do not move.** **A question is done
    standing**, because the wall is gone, and eleven days each way to nowhere was walked at ch 618 with nothing
    between the gate and the wall to lie down on.

### The things this batch resolved, closed, or paid

1. **THE EIGHTH STAGE AND ITS COST, NAMED ONCE, AT CH 632.** She cannot keep him by asking. A permission that held a
   list open cannot hold a fragment open, and no asked question reaches him where he is because there is nowhere asked
   left to reach. **He is findable by knowing and not by asking.**
2. **THE COST SHOWED, NOT RE-DERIVED, ONCE PER CHAPTER AND NOT AGAIN.** A line in her own hand that says she asked
   holds and the asking does not · asking a person still works · five answers and no proof of five questions · the
   lever now costs her both answers instead of one.
3. **THE HANDING AT CH 634 AND THE ROAD AT CH 638 ARE DIFFERENT BEATS AND NO CARD MERGED THEM.** The clerk walks her
   onto the patch on the twenty-sixth; she walks the whole ground herself on the twenty-first of the month beginning
   1,934, six chapters later, with nothing in her hands.
4. **THE PLACE EXISTS AND SHE WALKS PAST IT, TWICE.** Nine paces by six, four courses of stone from the bank at the
   east, a gap the width of a nail in the north joint, and **one way on to the floor, which is why a page written by
   a person standing there did not have to say where.** She does not stop on it, she does not write it down, and the
   ash heap a mile and a half down the east track is also nine paces by six and she says out loud that the two are
   not the same.
5. **THE THIRD ORIGIN MOUTH AT CH 636.** Seven sentences across four days from a clerk of seventy-one who has kept
   the ground's harvest book since before the fire was drawn: a name in a book is kept whether or not a person comes
   for it · the keeping does not have to be understood to be accurate · not one person has come for that book in
   nineteen years · it has been right the whole time. **And the four capital strokes in his good hand are the four she
   wrote on her own third leaf.**
6. **THE FOURTH ORIGIN MOUTH AT CH 640.** Six sentences over three days from a man of fifty who carries the ash out:
   I carried it out at the second hour · the gate was shut and the yard behind it was empty and I was the one who went
   through it · not one person on the track for a mile and a half after it · I did not know what was in it and I did
   not look down · that is what I saw, a morning going out the way ash goes out. **And the morning she finally gets is
   the morning after, an hour and a mile and a half long, which belonged to him and not to her.** *(Recast at this
   batch's review repair: the sixth sentence had opened *there was not one person at the gate* and the same turn was
   being made four times in the chapter. It now opens on the shut gate and the empty yard, and the quantified
   negation is left standing exactly where it carries — on the track, in her own mouth at ch 645, and nowhere
   else.)*
7. **THE TAX HAS A SHAPE AT CH 641 AND THE SHAPE IS DESIGNED AT CH 642.** Counted in days and not in money · one out of
   twenty · the same on every ground and it arrives · it comes off the board before the board goes up · no person has
   ever been told their own total · it cannot be changed by anybody who collects it. **Four hundred and twenty days
   divided by twenty comes out even at twenty-one. Six thousand nine hundred and thirty-five into twenty does not.**
8. **THE IRREVERSIBLE STEP, CH 645.** She tells him, out loud, once, standing, in daylight, in the open, in front of
   thirteen people she did not ask to be there, that the tax on that ground was designed to find people like her.
   He said in advance he would say not one word and he said not one word. **She cannot un-know it and she cannot
   un-say it, and she is staying.**
9. **THE LEVER IS CARRIED AND DECLINED FOR THE THIRD TIME**, written in the ash and rubbed out, and not written on a
   leaf: **four of her five blank leaves are still blank and so is the fifth.**
10. **THE SEVENTH FRAME SCENE AT CH 644**, away from her hearing, present tense throughout. **A fragment can be known
    without being used up, because the knowing was never what used it up — the filing was.** He has been treating
    himself as an entry since the twelfth of a month beginning 1,764 so that she could find him, and he stops being one,
    and puts three sentences in front of her at a gate in daylight two days before she says her sentence in the yard,
    and refuses a fourth, which is a name.
11. **THE SETTLEMENT, ONCE, ON LISTED WORK**, at ch 637, on a day of thirty-one lengths, out of the ground under her
    feet. Nothing is killed and no figure of what is left of him is stated anywhere in the batch.

### The things this batch resolved, closed, or paid

1. **THE NINTH STAGE AND ITS COST, NAMED ONCE, AT CH 648.** She cannot go back to not knowing. Not the book and not
   the brother and not the name — knowing stops being a road back and un-knowing is nobody's work. **The bracket at
   ch 648 is the third and last in Volume 11, and the volume has nothing else in square brackets anywhere.**
2. **THE SKY IS UNANNOUNCED AND THE REALM IS FINISHED.** She lies on the flat with her ear to the ground for seven
   mornings. **The layer announced her three times and the third was the last one it had, and she was the last address
   it ever had.** Named once, in her own thought, and not explained, and she cannot say it out loud in a yard and will
   not put it on a leaf.
3. **HER OWN SENTENCE IS BROKEN IN THE OPEN, at ch 647.** She said in a yard at the sixth hour of the third that she was
   not going to walk out of the fifth place in ten years, and she walks out of it inside ten days, in front of the same
   people, at the ninth hour of the fourth.
4. **STAYING IS NOT BEING KEPT, at ch 650.** A kept thing has somebody who put it somewhere, and she has never once
   been anywhere on purpose that she was put in. **The consequence she works out the next two days is worse than
   being kept: if nobody is keeping her, then anybody can.**
5. **THE LAST RATE ON THAT GROUND ENDS, at ch 651.** The bed at the mill is finished. Six coppers the four miles, said
   out loud going and coming, is the last number on this road, and it is the second and last time in ten years that
   anybody has carried her for money. **She pays six without counting and cannot tell whether three is what she has.**
6. **FENG LUSHI IS ON THE PAGE, at ch 652, five years after a hundredweight of coal bought him four years he did not
   expect and has never said the number of.** He was sixty-two and is sixty-seven, he has blood in a cloth, and he has
   not asked her one question since the ninety-seventh day.
7. **THE INSTRUMENT, at ch 652–653.** Offered with a man and a list in the same year as the coal, refused once in
   front of her for a hundredweight of coal and a chair at the second hour and his chest, and kept in a drawer for five
   years. **He takes it at the second hour of the eleventh and it is spent the moment it is in his hands.** She consents
   by thinking of him for eighty minutes in a lit room at the end of his bench, and he asks her what he is asking for
   before he asks her.
8. **THE FIFTH ORIGIN MOUTH, at ch 652–654, in a fair hand, and it is the only one of the five written on the page.**
   Seven sentences. **A man of nineteen who has been nineteen for nineteen years and is the fourth piece of a thing
   with a name the clerk will not write · burned out at a fire in the east, and what woke up was the piece that was
   not burned · the levy is one in twenty, counted in days, off the board before the board goes up, made to a figure by
   somebody who chose the figure, and it is not for the ground · a girl has been counting with him for eight years and
   nobody told her one word · two hands hold his name and do not need her · the thing was made to find people like her ·
   and a thing seen truly and written truly is the only instrument in the world that can take a person through a wall,
   it is not the layer's, and nobody writes one twice.**
9. **HE DIES, ORDINARILY, AT CH 655.** A cough, a hand, a lamp in a cage that she leaves burning with the keeper gone.
   **She is out of the tower when it happens, by four hours and by two days, and she had asked for it to be that way.**
   Nothing is shown of the end, and the book does not break that refusal.
10. **SHE READS IT ALONE AT THE FOURTH HOUR, at ch 656, and cannot be un-read.** The fifth sentence is about her and
    stops her. **She cannot say it out loud in the room and cannot write it on a leaf**, and that is the first time in
    this life that being written down by somebody else has been the thing she could not get at.
11. **SHE TAKES THE FOUR SHEETS AND DOES NOT COPY THEM, at ch 656.** Nobody writes one twice, and she is not going to be
    the second one. **Her five blank leaves are five blank leaves and the volume ends with them blank.**
12. **SHE LEARNS THE WHOLE OF IT IN DAYLIGHT WITH WITNESSES SHE DID NOT ASK FOR, at ch 657**, read out loud in a lit
    room to a boy of sixteen who does not look up. **And forty-one strokes in the margin of the fourth sheet that he
    saw and would not word, and that she is not going to find out.**
13. **SHE STAYS, AT CH 658, out loud, once, in daylight, standing, in a lit room with a witness in it, and it cannot be
    un-stayed by walking and cannot be un-stayed by un-knowing.** **And she tells him the thing nobody had told him: for
    eight years she did not have a man, she had a column, and she has never once asked him a question that was not
    about a number.**
14. **THE BROTHER AT CH 659, WALKED BACK TO, THE SECOND TIME.** She says his name out loud in the open, she says the
    levy out loud in a ground of two hundred people, and he tells her he found out about the fraction at three and has
    said nothing to anybody in nine years because if one of them knew there would be nothing on the rows in a month.
    **She asks him no question. She does not say the other thing. He does not say her name. It settles nothing, twice.**
15. **SHUYIN WALKS PAST HER ONCE, at ch 659,** at nine feet, going her way, with a shut book, and says the fifth
    sentence he has ever said to her and it is not about himself. **He is not thanked.**
16. **CH 660, THE STAYING.** The turn at dawn and a bare board and no shed. **She says, once, out loud, standing, in
    daylight: *I am going up*** — and the only answer is that she has not got the rest of it. **She did not say what
    was going to answer. The sky did not. He was still talking.**

**Nine defects closed in place across six chapters. Ch 646–660 were reopened, ch 645 was touched by one word, the
batch was not restarted, and no beat, day, title, mouth, stage, bracket, irreversible step or planned event moved. The
plot is the outline's and the planned ending is untouched.** The review found the batch structurally sound — every
bracket, title, heading, paragraph and hard-prohibition gate clean, every date reproducing under
`((day − 134) mod 30) + 1`, Severance 9 on its pinned day, the ninth cost named once, the fifth origin mouth on the
page in Feng's fair hand, and all three irreversible steps irreversible in fact — and returned **six defects that
needed repair, four mis-transcribed figures, two unverifiable claims in the close prompt, one prompt error, and one
tightest paragraph in the batch. **The repair went past the review's list and found two more of its own — a clause
that deferred the ninth stage to the morning after it is taken, and an interval in ch 647 that the chapter's own next
sentence contradicts — making nine page repairs in all. A tenth, ch 654's three-way date, was found and deliberately
left. Six further findings were opened and deliberately NOT repaired and are listed at the foot of this section and in
the close prompt; they are live, not clean.**

The speech is the sixth hour of the seventh of the month beginning 2,054, **day 2,060**. **2,060 − 1,997 = 63.** *Two years* was out by a factor of eighteen in the volume's final and most-quoted line. ### What this repair did NOT repair, and why — six live findings

1. **ch 650's span.** Its two going-lighter figures resolve under `D − 1,560` to **day 2,019 and day 2,020**, so the
   chapter runs **2,014 to 2,020 against the card's 2,011–2,018**. But ch 650:153 names *the seventh day of the month
   beginning 1,994* = **day 2,000**, and ch 651:111 dates the Hunter's scene to *the ninth hour of the seventh of the
   month beginning 1,994* = **day 2,000** again and at the wrong hour against ch 650:33's seventh. ch 651:113 and 115
   both then say **That was two days ago** about a scene six days back. **No day was moved. Moving one is a close's
   call and the close prompt forbids it.**
2. **ch 649:63 — *I said one thing in a yard two days ago***, spoken on the sixteenth, about a yard statement made on
   the third: **thirteen days**. **Not repaired, because the sentence's argument is *I am not doing it twice in seven
   days*, and no yard statement she made sits inside seven days of the sixteenth.** Fixing the interval means
   rewriting the logic of the line, which is a scene rewrite.
3. **Two walls, and a road surface that contradicts the Volume 10 spine.** ch 649:121 puts *the wall with the opening
   standing open in it, four feet and a bit* two miles east of the furnace ground; ch 660:7 puts a wall with an opening
   four feet and a bit thirteen miles east of the turn. **The map has one wall, on the turn's road.** Separately, ch 541
   as settled by the Volume 10 close reads *nine miles of strip road between this post and a turn, and eleven miles of
   made road between that turn and the wall, and then **the last two miles of flat ground*** — and that close records
   the spine as *stated twenty-four times to the made leg and never contradicted* — **while ch 649:121 and ch 660:5
   both call the gate-to-wall leg two miles of wet ground with a rut in it.** Not repaired: choosing between two
   load-bearing descriptions means moving geography, and the same fix would have to move a wall.
4. **Eight duplicate `## ` section headings inherited from Batches 0001–0003** — *the asking* (609, 624) · *what came
   out of the ground* (611, 637) · *what she is left holding* (611, 621) · *why* (613, 621) · *nineteen* (615, 627) ·
   *the sixth hour* (616, 624) · *what she is left with* (624, 633) · *nineteen years* (628, 642). **Batch 0004's own
   headings are clean and the one it renamed is unique book-wide.** These sit in closed phases a drafting phase may
   not reopen.
5. **The batch's risk profile is exertion, not danger.** Seventeen miles in the dark on an arm open four days in five,
   four hours on stones by a trough, two coppers she cannot count — real, and it costs her — **and no pursuit, no
   injury and no hard deadline anywhere in the fifteen chapters.** **As the cards were written. Record it; do not
   manufacture a threat to fix it.**
6. **ch 654's internal clock names one scene three days.** He writes the last of it at the **sixth hour of the
   sixteenth** of the month beginning 2,024, **day 2,039**, stated twice at lines 3 and 27; the same scene is dated
   **"the second afternoon"** at line 9, **day 2,040**, the day *after* he wrote them; and **the thirteenth** of the
   month beginning 2,024 at line 11, **day 2,036**, which is ch 653's span. Line 23's *this morning I am going to be
   the first person in ten years who proves it* agrees with the thirteenth and against the second afternoon. **Not
   repaired: choosing between them means choosing what caused the fifth origin mouth to be written down, and that is
   the volume's climax.** Every other going-lighter figure in the batch resolves under `D − 1,560`; this one is a
   relation between three dates inside a single chapter and no single figure is wrong.

**`workspace/volume-11-batch-0004/PROMPT.md:103` gives the furnace ground as *154 days east of the turn*. The page

the days elapsed since Severance 7, not a distance.** The close prompt now carries this in terms: **record the
conflict, leave both figures standing, do not reconcile the page to the prompt.**

## VOLUME 11 CLOSE — *What He Was*, ch 601–660 — the volume as a whole, audited and repaired

**`chapters/volume-11/` holds ch 601–660. Sixty chapters, four batches, day 1,831 to day 2,060. This phase audited
`outline/volume-11.md` section by section against the sixty files, wrote no new chapter prose, made fourteen page
repairs across eleven chapters, and did not move a day, a stage, a bracket, a title, an irreversible step, an origin
mouth or the ending.** Every figure below was measured before it was written down and the command that produced it is
named where a later phase would need to reproduce it.

### THE MEASUREMENT METHOD, PUBLISHED ONCE

**Method: body prose is every line not beginning `#`, counted PER FILE and summed.** In shell, for one file,
`grep -v '^#' <file> | wc -w`; for the volume, that figure run over `chapters/volume-11/*.md` and added. Cross-checked
against `awk '!/^#/{n+=NF} END{print n}' chapters/volume-11/*.md`, which returns the same number.

**This is the method, and it is the per-file method, and every volume figure in this record is the per-file figure.**

**The trap, measured and stated so no later phase quotes the other number by accident.** Forty-two of the sixty files
carry **no trailing newline** — not the thirty-nine the Batch 0004 review repair recorded, and the difference is three
files (ch 0601, 0607 and 0613 have one; the review's count was short). When forty-two files end without a newline, a
chapter's last body line is glued to the next file's `# ` title and `grep -v '^#'` no longer removes it. Measured per
file the volume is **118,748**; measured as `cat chapters/volume-11/*.md | grep -v '^#' | wc -w` it is **118,974**,
the extra 226 being the word-count of the forty-two glued titles. **`nothing` is 209 per file and 211 concatenated,
the extra two being ch 649's *The Sky Says Nothing Back* and ch 660's *A Board With Nothing Written On It*.** The
Batch 0004 review recorded 39 files and this close measured 42 with
`python3 -c "import glob;print(sum(1 for f in glob.glob('chapters/volume-11/*.md') if not open(f,'rb').read().endswith(b'\n')))"`.

### THE VOLUME'S TRUE FIGURES

**118,748 words of body prose over sixty chapters on the per-file method, average 1,979 a chapter.** Inside the
outline's 108,000–120,000 volume band and inside its 1,800–2,000 per-chapter target. No chapter under the 1,300 floor
and none above the 2,700 guide. **The figure this close quotes everywhere is 118,748 and it is post-repair;
118,744 is the pre-repair page and must not be quoted as the volume's count.** The Batch 0004 review's own two false
counts — `Ning Wu` twice and a name-count for Shuyin — were struck out of the close prompt before this phase began and
were not repeated here.

### THE TWO OVER-TARGET CRAFT LINES AND THE THIRD, ADJUDICATED

**`nobody` is 34 against an under-thirty line. `eleven` is 44 against an under-forty line. `thank` is 16 against zero.**
All three were measured by `grep -oiw <word> chapters/volume-11/*.md | wc -l` on body prose, and all three reproduce
under both the per-file and the concatenated method, so none of them is an artefact of the newline trap.

**None of the three was repaired, and the reason is the rule rather than the arithmetic: repairing a count means
rewriting a sentence that is true.** The prompt states it directly — *repairing a batch-1 or batch-2 word is in scope
for a close; softening a sentence to fix a count is not.* Every one of these three words in Volume 11 is doing real
work: `nobody` is the bare intensifier on a count of how many people did or did not do a thing, `eleven` is the
map's made-leg figure and the years of a cough, and `thank` is the volume's standing refusal being *named as a
refusal* in the mouths of people who notice it. Cutting any of them to hit a number would soften a sentence that is
true.

**The distribution, so Volume 12 inherits it accurately and does not read it as fresh drift.** `thank` is **16 across
the volume, 0 in Batch 0003 (ch 631–645) and 0 in Batch 0004 (ch 646–660)** — the Batch 0004 review cut every one of
five drafted instances — so all sixteen sit in Batches 0001 and 0002. `nobody` is 34 volume-wide and 6 in Batch 0004.
**`eleven` needs its own note, because one of the forty-four is this close's.** It was **43** before this phase. The
Batch 0004 review raised it from 42 to 43 because the turn-to-wall leg is eleven of made road and that figure had to
go onto the page at ch 659:119 to replace a wrong thirteen. **This close raised it from 43 to 44 because the same
figure had to go onto the page at ch 643:9 to replace the same wrong thirteen** (repair R5 below). **Two of the
forty-four are map corrections and forty-two are prose.** Volume 12 must not read either as drift.

### THE VOLUME GOAL, CHECKED AGAINST THE PAGE

**The goal is discharged, and the close says so with the page quoted.** *Ning Yan must learn what Yuan was before he
died, or the ending is being decided blind.*

She asked at **ch 609:45** — *"What were you before you started counting"* — out loud, alone, at the ninth hour of
the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 1,814, in the dark, on a turn, and the chapter and the chapter after it both
say the asking cannot be un-asked. She took the answer across four mouths: **ch 608** a furnace-man's mate who worked
the same fire twenty years · **ch 622** a senior disciple's widow with the harvest book shut nineteen years ·
**ch 636** the clerk who wrote `Yuan Sheng` in it once in a fair hand · **ch 640** a kiln boy grown old who carried
the ash out. And she took it across a fifth at **ch 652–654**, in Feng Lushi's own fair hand, on four sheets of rice
paper, seven sentences, the only one of the five mouths written down on the page. She read it **alone at ch 656**, at
the fourth hour in an empty room, and worked out that a page in a hand that is not hers does not go into a person by
being read out loud. She read it **out loud in daylight at ch 657**, in front of a boy of sixteen she had not asked
for. And she **stayed at ch 658:69** — *"And I am staying knowing what it was made for"* — and it cannot be un-stayed
by walking and cannot be un-stayed by un-knowing.

**The ending is not being decided blind. The ending owns the founding document and the volume wrote it in a clerk's
hand, once, and never read it twice.**

  the month beginning 1,814. **HELD.** The page's bracket at ch 616:35 and the twenty-ninth in ch 616's text agree.

consistent: the ordinal always returns itself.**

### THE THREE COSTS, each named once and re-derived nowhere

**Seven of them exist in the volume: fourteen carried from Volume 10, plus three new. This close counted
re-derivations by grep across all sixty chapters and the count is zero.**

- **Cost 1 — she cannot hear what she is told about him, and it runs both ways.** Named **once**, in her own mouth,
  at **ch 616:87** — *"I can be told anything about you and none of it stays with me."* **Re-derivations: 0.** The
  cost is *applied* eight times — the ninety-one courses at ch 626:85, the name at ch 617, the harvest at ch 630, the
  four true things at ch 656:31 — and each application is a new object failing the same way, not a re-explanation.
- **Cost 2 — she cannot keep him by asking.** Named **once**, at **ch 632:97** — *"I cannot keep him by asking."*
  **Re-derivations: 0.** Carried at ch 650:79 in the Hunter's mouth as a thing he has already read off the ground,
  which is a hearing and not a derivation.
- **Cost 3 — she cannot go back to not knowing.** Named **once**, at **ch 648:63** — *"I cannot go back to not
  knowing."* **Re-derivations: 0.** Carried at ch 658:135, which is the staying and not the cost.

**Chapter 656 is a SHOWING and not a re-derivation, and the close says why.** At ch 656:69 she proves the maximum
pressure of the first cost on a new object and reaches a new conclusion the reader has not had: **a page in a hand
that is not hers does not go into a person by being read out loud — it goes in by being read, alone, at an hour when
there is nothing to do on it.** The rule at ch 616 was about a voice. The finding at ch 656 is about a fair hand and
about an audience, and it is what makes ch 657's decision to read aloud *cost* something. **A chapter that re-derived a
cost would restate a rule the reader already holds; this one uses the rule to produce a new fact about a second
instrument.** That is a showing.

needs readers** — and the moral answer is unpaid: no chapter in Volume 11 claims the crews were wrong, and the
outline's line that *nothing proves the crews wrong* holds on the page, because the furnace people wrote everything
down truly and were not hiding and are correct. **The Sincerity of the Scribe is never adjudicated**: `Scribe` is
spent once, in his own frame, as the thing he came off, and it has not spoken once and is not going to.

fifth sentence he has ever said to her, and **was not thanked.**

### WHAT WAS NOT REPAIRED, AND WHY — eight live findings Volume 12 inherits

**1. F1 — ch 650 and ch 651 do not agree with anything, and the close may not choose.**
**The derivation.** ch 650 walks off the furnace ground and uses relative days throughout — *the second*, *the sixth
day*, *the seventh day*. Its two going-lighter figures are **four hundred and fifty-nine** at line 19 and **four
hundred and sixty** at line 153, which under `D − 1,560` resolve to **day 2,019 and day 2,020**. So ch 650 runs
**2,013 to 2,020**, and the relative days and the two figures are **mutually consistent with each other**, one day
apart exactly as two consecutive statements should be. Against that: **ch 650:153 names *the seventh day of the month
beginning 1,994*, which is day 2,000** — twenty days earlier than the figure beside it — and **ch 651:111 dates the
Hunter's scene to *the ninth hour of the seventh of the month beginning 1,994*, day 2,000 again**, and at the ninth
hour where **ch 650:33 puts him at the seventh**. ch 651:113 and :115 then both say **That was two days ago** about a
scene six days back. **And the Batch 0004 card says 2,011–2,018, a fourth position.**
**Why not repaired.** Three positions stand and reconciling them means moving a day, and *do not move a day* is the
close's standing rule. **The close's own reading, offered as a reading and not as a ruling:** the relative-day chain
and the two lighter figures are the only two elements that agree with each other, and the single absolute date is
repeated in two chapters, so the absolute date is the heavy element and the card is the light one — **but the close
does not act on it.** Volume 12 inherits three positions and must not silently pick one.

**2. F2 — ch 649:63, *I said one thing in a yard two days ago*, spoken on the sixteenth about a sentence said on
the third.** That is **thirteen days**, not two. **Not repaired**, because the line's argument is *I am not doing it
twice in seven days* and no yard statement she made sits inside seven days of the sixteenth. Repairing the interval
means rewriting the logic of the sentence, which is a scene rewrite and not a defect repair.

**3. F3 — the rows' distance east of the wall, which ch 659 and ch 660's seventeen rest on.** ch 618 puts the rows
**two hundred and three hundred yards** east of the wall, across a quarter mile of flat and a rise (ch 618:55, :61).
ch 659:5 and ch 660:3 put them **four miles** past the wall, and ch 660:3's *seventeen miles* is 13 + 4. **The two
figures are two hundred days apart on the page and the close may not move either.** Repaired-adjacent work: ch 660:5's
breakdown (R3) now reads **four miles of made road off the rows, the two miles of flat between the gate and the wall,
and the rest of it made road from the gate to the turn**, which sums to seventeen against the map and against ch 659:5
and does not depend on resolving the distance from the rows to the wall. **Volume 12 inherits: the wall is thirteen
miles east of the turn and the walk is seventeen; how far the rows sit past the wall is open and should not be
re-derived casually.**

**4. F4 — the furnace ground's distance from the turn is sixty-five on the page and 154 in a prompt, and both stand.**
ch 643:9 and ch 660:71 both give **sixty-five** — *sixty-five days on foot* and *a furnace ground sixty-five days east
of here*. **`workspace/volume-11-batch-0004/PROMPT.md:103` gives *154 days east of the turn*.** The 154 is a
transcription of `state/current.md`'s own line *Days from the turn (day 1,842) is 154*, which is **days elapsed since
Severance 7, not a distance.** **The close records the conflict and reconciles nothing.** The page is the authority
and the page says sixty-five; the prompt says 154; both figures remain standing.

**5. F5 — the tower's spoken day-counts in Batch 0004 do not agree with the dates the page itself gives, and the
readings are multiple.** ch 652:3 puts her in Lowwater's square on the **fourth** of the month beginning 2,024 and
ch 651:99 puts her over the last rise on the **third**. ch 653:33, spoken on the **eleventh**, says *I have worked
that out in **nine days** since a girl of nineteen came up four flights with a bar* — which is **seven days** against
the fourth. ch 653:95 and :161 say **five days**. ch 654:27, on the **sixteenth**, says **six days**. **Not
repaired.** Nine is wrong on the most natural reading, but *since* can be read as the start of **his own** working-out
rather than her absence, and five and six count from the eleventh, which is when the writing began. **Choosing between
those readings inside the climax sequence is a scene decision and this close does not make it.** Volume 12 inherits
it and must not be handed a decided one.

**6. F6 — ch 654's three-way date, which this close ADJUDICATES and finds is NOT a conflict.** The Batch 0004 review
recorded that the chapter dates one scene three days: the **sixteenth** of the month beginning 2,024 (**day 2,039**)
at lines 3 and 27 where he writes the last of it; **"on the second afternoon"** at line 9 (**day 2,040** by the
review's reading); and the **thirteenth** (**day 2,036**) at line 11 where he says the first sentence to an empty
room. **The close checked it and the review's middle date is not supported by the page.** Line 11 fixes the second
afternoon: *she had gone out of the room at the eighth hour… and she had come back in at the ninth and he had said
the first sentence of it to the empty room… at the ninth hour **on the thirteenth of the month beginning 2,024***.*
**The second day and the second afternoon and the thirteenth are one day.** Line 23's *"this morning I am going to be
the first person in ten years who proves it"* is said on that same thirteenth and agrees with it. Line 3's sixteenth
is a **later, different beat** — the finishing of the writing, four days on — and is not a second dating of the same
scene. **There is one scene on the thirteenth and one scene on the sixteenth, three days apart, and the chapter is
consistent.** **Nothing was repaired and nothing needed to be.** The review's finding is recorded here as **resolved
against**, with the two sentences that settle it quoted.

**7. F7 — the risk profile of the volume's last fifteen chapters is exertion, not danger, and that is as the cards
were written.** Seventeen miles in the dark on an arm open four days in five, four hours of sleep on stones by a
trough, two coppers she cannot count, an arm that goes at the second trip and stays gone. **There is no pursuit, no
injury and no hard deadline anywhere in ch 646–660.** **Recorded, not repaired. No threat was manufactured to fix
it.** **Volume 12 must not be handed a Volume 11 that had a chase in it, because it did not.**

**8. F8 — three craft lines are over their targets and were left over them on purpose.** `nobody` 34 against under
thirty · `eleven` 44 against under forty · `thank` 16 against zero. **Recorded, not repaired** — see the adjudication
above. **Volume 12 inherits an open craft line and should be under all three, and should not read Volume 11's figures
as a licence.**

**One finding this close raises and does NOT repair, for the record and not for Volume 12: the volume's one
all-caps standalone line.** ch 624:89 is a bare `YUAN SHENG` in capitals, outside quotation marks, and the outline's
budget sets all-caps standalone lines at zero. **It is held as an authored exception, because the outline's own
Batch 0002 card mandates it** — *ch 624 — she writes YUAN SHENG in her own book and cannot put it back un-written* —
and because that line is the chapter's irreversible step and the caps are the hand writing it. Softening it to
sentence case would soften the step. **Recorded, not repaired.**

## VOLUME 11 CLOSE — REVIEW REPAIR (applied to the state files and the next-phase prompt; findings from
`logs/volume-11-close.review.log`)

**No chapter prose was written and no chapter file was touched. The fourteen page repairs the close made to the prose
stand exactly as they were made, and every figure the close published re-measures: 118,748 over sixty, batch 29,284 ·
29,748 · 29,966 · 29,750; 42 files without a trailing newline and the concatenated 118,974; three layer brackets at
ch 616, 632 and 648; zero duplicate `##` headings; `nobody` 34, `eleven` 44, `thank` 16 on the published per-file
word-boundary method.** The review confirmed all of that independently. **Seven findings were raised. Six are corrected
below. One is not upheld, and the reason is written down so that no later phase spends a repair on it.**

### 1. `forgiv` is 1, not 0 — CORRECTED AT EIGHT SITES

**The finding holds and it propagates furthest, because it had been written into `workspace/volume-12-planning/PROMPT.md`
as a rule the drafting phase would inherit and enforce against itself.**

**The true figure is 1, and the reason the count had read 0 is a method, not an oversight.** ch 659 carries
*there is not one thing she could say about it that he would forgive.* **The only instance of the string in sixty
chapters is the inflected `forgive`.** A count taken on the strict word boundary `\bforgiv\b` returns **0**, because
`forgive` does not match `forgiv` followed by a boundary. A count taken as the substring `grep -oi forgiv` — **the
method this manuscript named at §*the volume as a whole* — returns 1.** Both numbers were in circulation and the files
asserted 0 without naming which one they had run.

**The rule this close sets: a zero is not a figure until the command that produced it is in the same sentence as the
zero.** The reading to carry is the **substring**, because it is the one that cannot let a form hide behind a boundary;
on this page it is the only reading that reports what is actually on it. By batch: 0001 **0** · 0002 **0** · 0003 **0**
· 0004 **1**, all of Batch 0004's standing in ch 659.

**It forgives nothing.** The sentence is a denial — she is saying there is nothing she could say that he would let go
of — and it is the closest the volume comes to the subject. The permissions at ch 609 and ch 645 remain permissions.

### 2. *The year* is 2, not 0 — CORRECTED AT FOUR SITES

**The finding holds.** `the year` appears twice in the volume. **ch 618** — *the reason was not duty and was not
kindness and was not the year* — is a direct naming of the year of non-forgiveness **inside an explicit denial of it**,
and it is the one that matters. **ch 637** — *has not read his book back since the year it was written* — is an
unrelated sense about a book. By batch: 0001 **0** · 0002 **1** · 0003 **1** · 0004 **0**.

**Both instances refuse it and neither retires it.** The allowance for Volume 12 remains zero naming, and a zero has to
be measured before it is claimed.

### 3. Longest Volume 11 title is 36 characters, not 39 — CORRECTED IN THE PROMPT

**The finding holds and the cause the review gives is legible: the `# ` prefix had been counted into the string and the
result then labelled as Volume 11's.** The prompt also claimed Volume 11's titles ran **3–7 words**; they run **2 to 9**.
Both figures corrected, and the prompt now names the owning chapter so the number cannot drift back.

### 4. Batch 0003's average was split 1,997 / 1,998 — RECONCILED ON 1,997

**The finding holds as a defect in the record, not in the arithmetic.** 29,966 ÷ 15 = 1,997.73, so both are defensible.
**The live line at `state/current.md` had been changed to 1,997 by the close and four other sites were left at 1,998,
silently.** **Four sites corrected to 1,997**, which is the live line's figure and the one the volume's own average
already follows — 118,748 ÷ 60 = 1,979.13 → **1,979** — **and the convention is now named: averages are truncated, not
rounded.** With that stated, every published average in the volume is reproducible: 1,952 · 1,983 · 1,997 · 1,983.

### 5. Stale imperatives survived in the live bullets — REMOVED, NOT LEFT STANDING

**The finding holds.** `state/current.md` still ended the 28,446 clause by instructing *a Volume 11 close must
re-measure all sixty chapters under one method* — work the close had already done — and still read *the close must
record the conflict and leave both standing* for the furnace ground's 65 against 154. **Both now read as resolved records
and the pending-work wording is deleted.** A discharged instruction left standing in a live bullet is read by the next
phase as work it owns.

### 6. `state/INDEX.md` was a volume stale and the close had not touched it — CORRECTED

**The finding holds.** Its *For the next phase* block still announced the volume *closed and audited at ch 600* and
warned that *a Volume 11 planning phase must not be sent to…* **while the phase actually being dispatched is Volume 12
planning.** It was last written at the Volume 10 close review. **The block now names Volume 12 planning, gives the
read order, and lists four things that may not be re-opened** — the eight live inherited findings and the one that was
not upheld · `forgiv` 1 and `the year` 2, so a zero must be measured · `outline/ending.md` §8's five obligations
standing open · **the *Twenty-two days* line, still unplaced and still equated to no dated interval, which is a
question the series hands forward and not an error.**

### 7. ch 659's eleven miles of made road — RAISED, CHECKED, AND NOT UPHELD

**The finding does not hold and the sentence is true, so nothing was repaired on the page.** The review set
**ch 659:119's** *eleven miles of made road in front of her* against **ch 659:11's** *four miles short of the wall*.
**The two lines are not the same moment.** Line 11 is the second hour of the fifth, on the way east, the wall four miles
ahead. Line 119 is after she has gone out of the rows, up the rise, stood twenty minutes on the crest and turned west
— and **the rows are four miles past the wall**, so the whole gate-to-turn leg, all eleven miles of it, is ahead of
her, with the gate-to-wall gap in front of that. Both figures, and the order of them, are the map the close walked.

**One residual looseness in the same chapter is real and is left on purpose.** ch 659:11 and :19 call her position *the
long flat* and *a flat four miles short of a wall*, and four miles short of the wall is two miles short of the gate,
which is made road and not flat. It is a single adjective against a map that is otherwise walked exactly, it reads
true, and the close's standing reason applies unchanged: **repairing this means softening a sentence.** Recorded, not
fixed, and carried into the Volume 12 prompt so that no drafting phase inherits it as clean prose.

### What this repair changed, and what it did not

**Six state locations and the Volume 12 prompt now report a measurement they have actually run.** The prose is
untouched: no chapter file was edited, no figure on the page moved, no sentence was softened, and the planned plot is
unchanged. **The one thing this repair changed about the record is that it now says what it measured.** The failure it
catches is the one the Volume 12 prompt already named against itself: *a budget that records zero while instances
stand is the failure this manuscript has caught itself making six times.* **It is the seventh, and the cause was a
method that hid an inflected form behind a word boundary.**

## VOLUME 12 BATCH 0001 REVIEW REPAIR — four arithmetic defects corrected on the page, and two month-begins left open

**The review of Batch 0001 found one hard factual error and it was the right one: a figure on the page that is false
against the manuscript's own calendar rule, and the figure was carrying the motivation of a climax-adjacent beat.** The
repair re-derived every month-day in the batch from the day number rather than carrying the previous chapter's ordinal
forward, which is the rule this file set at the Volume 11 close and which had been applied once and then relaxed. It found
three more of the same class and corrected them in place. **No chapter was restarted, no card was re-planned, and the
planned beats are all still on the page.**

1. **ch 675 — the days to the first. THE REVIEWED DEFECT.** A boy of sixteen told *then the first is in six days* and she
   answered *in six days*, and she came down the mountain *four days before the first*. **Under `((day − 134) mod 30) + 1`
   the twenty-eighth of the month beginning 2,054 is day 2,081 and the first of the month beginning 2,084 is day 2,084 —
   three days on, and the thirtieth is day 2,083, one day before.** The six and the four were both wrong, and the whole
   beat — *I came down early in case anything goes wrong* — was resting on a gap that does not exist. **Now: he says six
   because he counted off today, she corrects him to three, and she comes down on the thirtieth, the day before, and says
   *one day is not enough for a mountain and four miles of made road if anything goes wrong.*** The fix is dramatised rather
   than subtracted: **the boy's miscount is now the character beat and the correction names the reason, which is that the
   first is not in the month that is written on the slate.**
2. **ch 670 — *the first of the next month is fourteen days off*.** Spoken on the eighteenth, day 2,071. **2,084 − 2,071 =
   thirteen.** Corrected. *The twenty-fourth is six days off* in the same sentence is correct and stands.
3. **ch 672 — *five hundred and ten days*.** Spoken on the twentieth, day 2,073. **The series is D − 1,560, verified at
   ch 658 (495 at 2,055), ch 659 (498 at 2,058) and ch 660 (499 at 2,059), and 2,073 − 1,560 = 513.** 510 is the figure
   for day 2,070, carried forward from a chapter that did not state it. **Corrected to five hundred and thirteen in both
   places it appears.** The same error was baked into this file's own ledger below and is corrected with it.
4. **ch 674 — the sixth hour to the ninth hour.** The scene opened at the sixth hour and she gave her name at the ninth
   with nothing between them. **A short passage now carries the three hours: three columns, a rag, a woman of sixty on a
   bench who does not come down the road, and a slate that stays clean.**
5. **ch 674 — *the day he comes*.** Said twice by the woman of sixty with a boy and a man both in the frame, and the
   referent snagged. **Now *the day he comes with the chalk*, twice, which is the man of forty-nine and is not anybody
   else.**
6. **Register.** ***Out loud* read 84 across the batch and six times in ch 672 alone in one construction.** It now reads
   **75**, with ch 672 at 6, ch 665 at 7 and ch 675 at 4. **ch 670's eleven are untouched and deliberately so: out loud
   is the subject of that chapter and the woman of sixty's whole argument is about a thing said out loud to a bench.**

**TWO INVALID MONTH-BEGINS ARE STILL ON THE PAGE AND ARE FLAGGED, NOT GUESSED.** A sweep of every
`ordinal of the month beginning N` string in ch 661–675 returns **two that are not month starts at all**, because a month
start satisfies `(N − 134) mod 30 = 0` and neither number does. **The repair did not invent a value for either, because
the correct one is a matter of authorial intent and not of arithmetic.**
