**A note the next phase inherits about how these numbers were made, because the manuscript has caught itself making the
zero-while-instances-stand error six times and this batch nearly made it a seventh.** Two of the zeros above were **not**
zero when the first draft was written and were caught only by re-measuring after the fact: the thirteen straight
apostrophes, the eight `about four seconds`, the eleven scaffolding instances, one `thank you`, one named weekday
(*Tuesday*, at ch 674, written into a woman's mouth as a hesitation and cut within the hour), and **one date out by a day
in each of ch 670, ch 671 and ch 672, caught by re-deriving `((day − 134) mod 30) + 1` per chapter rather than carrying
the previous chapter's ordinal forward.** **The rule that follows: derive every month-day from the day number, never
from the previous chapter's ordinal, and re-measure every zero on the finished files before writing it into a state
file.** A zero written before the measurement is a promise, not a figure.

**AND THE RULE WAS NOT CARRIED, WHICH IS WHY THE BATCH 0001 REVIEW REPAIR EXISTED.** **Re-deriving a month-day is not the
same job as deriving an interval, and the batch did the first and skipped the second.** Every ordinal on the page was
correct — the chapters said *the first of the month beginning 2,084* and that is the right first — **and then the
sentence that counted the days to that first said six, and four, and both were wrong.** The same happened to a lighter
figure and to a second interval in ch 670. **Three of the four were found only by a reviewer who subtracted; none was
found by a writer who was checking that the label was a real month.** **The added rule, and it is the one that matters:
*an ordinal and the interval that reaches it are two different figures, and an interval must be subtracted from the day
number, not counted on fingers from the day before.* Verify every stated distance by subtraction, not by reading.** A
chapter that names the first of the next month three times in one scene has told you three times what the reader is
checking.

## What the batch established on the page, and what it may not re-derive

1. **The turn, the road, the tower and the frame are now a walked map.** The turn on the store road · the bench ·
   the two posts four hundred yards east of it with a slate let into a bar between two posts and a thumb-wide groove on
   three sides of the slate · a cottage four miles west at a stopped lime bed · a mill five miles west with a nine-foot
   oak wheel that has not turned in nine years · a post nine miles west of the turn · **a tower four miles up a mountain
   from the square at Lowwater: four flights to the copying floor, the short breath at the third landing, four hundred
   volumes, a rack that takes county paper and not a clerk's, a lamp in a cage on a shelf on the fourth landing, and a
   stair behind the shelves at the west end of the copying floor with four more flights above it.** **No distance
  between the tower and the turn is stated anywhere in ch 661–675, because the manuscript has never stated one.**
2. **The first half of the answer to the batch's question, said on the page in three sentences at ch 667.** An
   announcement is not made to be heard, it is made to arrive; if there is a person in the place it arrives and if there
   is not one it goes into the ground with no sign that it did not; it is not the announcement that has to be found, it
   is the room. **Nine times she was announced and nine times there was no room. That is now established fact and is not
   re-explained anywhere in ch 668–675.**
3. **The second half is addressed to a body, and neither of them has a body that can read it.** He says it at ch 667 and
   the finding is structural: the arriving needs a room, a person in the room and a hand; the boy's hand cannot be the
   one (ch 669) and Yuan's is not a hand at all; **so the instrument is her own, and it is a stub of a nib, a cake of ink
   opened on the seventh of the month beginning 1,874, and a hand that cannot write a false line.**
4. **The room at the top of the stair, as it now stands.** Four landings above the copying floor, a top step, a low door
   with flat close-set bars in the top half, a bar across it **on the landing side**, put there from the corridor by
   somebody who then went down and did not come back up. Inside: **a long table down the middle, nothing on it, a lamp on
   a shelf at the far end that is out, a candle stub gone into its dish, and no chairs.** Dust on the bar and on the
   sill of the same grey as the nine-year dust in the building: **shut since before she was ten years old.** The finding
   is at ch 668 and it is that **there is nothing to receive an announcement in it and no one to receive one, and those
   are one fact and not two.** **Nothing above the low door is described, and the batch spends no card on what shuts
   the bar.**
5. **A board, as it now stands.** It is a notice and not a wage; it goes up on the first of a month at the first hour on
   a cart with a piece of sacking over the slate and comes back down and is wiped with the flat of a thumb from left to
   right; **the fifth comes off the days in the column before it goes up and the person does not know what is left**;
   **a board is the only thing anybody has ever paid her for and it is the only thing the levy comes off, and it is one
   object and not two** (ch 672, said out loud on a public road in daylight with four people going past). A man of
   forty-nine comes out on the twenty-fourth of every month to take in what is on the slate. **The board at this turn
   has gone up with nothing on it since the eighteenth of the month beginning 1,814.**
6. **The woman of sixty's fact.** Her name went up on the second of a month beginning 1,806 and she was on that board
   for four of nineteen years working the road out of Lowwater; the west road stopped; a notice about a person who is
   not doing anything is a notice that gets walked past; **she has sat on that bench for nine years because it is where
   the board is and it is the only place she would be recognised in.** **She said it once and she does not say it
   again, and she is not going to tell her not to go on.**
7. **The batch's irreversible step, ch 674, in fact.** **`Ning Yan`, in chalk, in a county hand, in one line, with a
   stroke in front of it and thirty days of the month beginning 2,084 in the next column, written at the ninth hour of
   the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2,054 by a man of forty-nine who was doing his month's work.** She asked
   one question first and it was answered. **One in twenty of thirty is a day and a half and she said it out loud
   herself before he wrote a stroke.** The board went up on the first of the month beginning 2,084 and came back down
   empty and eleven people went past the frame in an hour and ten minutes and looked at nothing.
8. **The name, and who has it.** Four people now know she has a name on a board: the boy of sixteen, the carter of
   sixty-four, the woman of sixty, and the man of forty-nine. **The woman of sixty told her out loud, on the second day
   of the frame, that being seen is not a kindness, because a kindness goes both ways and a notice does not, and that
   the day the notice stops they stop.** That sentence is the moral pressure of Batch 0002 and it is **not softened and not
   withdrawn.**

Turn · thirteen miles east to a wall · a gate two miles short of it · two miles of flat between the gate and the wall with

13. **THE BILL FOR COURT, raised at ch 688 and NOT PAID.** A thing that reads records has never wanted one in eleven
    hundred years and there is one now. **She raises it out loud, standing, at the tenth hour of the nineteenth, and it is
    not answered by anybody, and she explicitly does not pay it and does not refuse it.** **Nothing in this batch addresses
    him but her. Nothing arrives with a sender. The address belongs to Volume 15.**
14. **THE PERMISSION, at ch 689, day 2,134, the twenty-first of the month beginning 2,114, at the third hour of the
    afternoon, standing, in daylight, at the north end of the rows, in front of about two hundred people, with six terms.**
    **THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE STEP.** She says **no** first and says it properly, and then changes it, and says why before
    she changes it. **She quotes the ch 658 sentence once, out loud, in a ground with people in it: *for eight years I did
    not have a man, I had a column.*** The six terms: **one thing at a time · in daylight · standing up · he says it out
    loud as he goes, before it is a line anywhere else · if he ever puts down one word that is not true she will know it
    inside a day and there is no road back for either of them · it is a record and not a hand, he does not decide anything,
    she decides everything.** The pinned sentence follows: **Yes, and you say it out loud as you go, and if you ever write a
    line down that is not true I will know inside a day and there is no road back for either of us.** **The reason she said
    yes is true, and the chapter says so out loud, and that is the damage.**
15. **CH 690 is what it is to live inside that.** Nothing goes wrong. The instrument is a voice and there is no page. **On
    the twenty-fifth of the month beginning 2,114 she notices she has stopped checking and does not remember deciding to.**
    **On the twenty-seventh he reads the entry about the permission itself out loud and she says nothing at all, because
    there is no seventh term, and a document agreed to in daylight cannot be added to either.** **She does not take it back
    and does not ask for the terms again.**
16. **The carter at the north end of the rows, ch 687.** A man of about fifty, nineteen years on that made road, never
    heard the name, does not know where he got it, got back on his cart and went east. **He is not named and is not on the
    page again.**
17. **Her brother is on the page once in this batch, at ch 678, in the third row, and settles nothing.** He is nineteen, six
    years in that ground, and the one thing he tells her is that **the board at the north end went from two lines to six to
    four** and that it has been four since the eleventh year. **He is not named on the page. `Ning Wu` reads 0.** **His one
    Volume 12 appearance outside ch 713 is spent here and the outline's own instruction — that both settle nothing — is
    kept.**
18. **The man with a shut notebook is on the page once, at ch 682, nine feet off, in the ordinary voice, and buys nothing
    and threatens nothing and is not asked a question.** She asks him one. He says it is not his question to decide and
    gives her the other thing. **`Hunter` 0, `field agent` 0, `Wall writ` 0. His request stays pending.**

## VOLUME 12 BATCH 0002 — REVIEW REPAIR

`logs/volume-12-batch-0002.review.log` audited ch 676–690, the state files and the Batch 0003 prompt. **It raised six hard
errors, two false state-file claims and four measured craft findings. All twelve are cleared on the page and recorded here.
The batch was not restarted, no card beat moved, no day moved, no title moved, no stage moved, and the planned ending and
the irreversible step at ch 689 stand exactly where the outline put them.**

### The six hard errors, each with what it was and what it is now

1. **THE STAGE'S LOCATION WAS CONTRADICTED IN THREE PLACES, AND IT IS THE OUTDOORS.** `ch 685` is canon: **Immortal Vessel 1
   was taken at the fourth hour of the afternoon on the fifteenth of the month beginning 2,114 at the north end of the rows,
   in the open, in daylight, in front of about two hundred people.** Three sentences elsewhere said a building with a hundred
   readers in it. **`ch 686` now says she was *not* in the room that time either and that there were two hundred people nine
   feet off and a bar lying along the ground; `ch 686`'s own recap now says *in the open, at the north end of two hundred rows
   of stones*; and `ch 689`, in Yuan's mouth, now says *at the north end of this ground in front of two hundred people and not
   one of them could put it anywhere*.** This mattered because the false version landed inside the batch's irreversible
   chapter, under a fifth term that reads *if you ever put down one word that is not true, I will know it inside a day*, in the
   same breath as *the reason I said yes is true*. **Nothing else moved: the chapter's finding is untouched — she is still
   the first person in this ground to go up a stage with nothing under it, and she is still unable to say a word about it to
   anybody, because of the question she asked standing up on a floor.**
2. **ONE EVENT, TWO AGES.** The refusal in the room with the shutters up is **`ch 474`, day 1,306, the third of the month
   beginning 1,304**, and ch 679 is day 2,094. **The interval is 788 days, which is two years and two months, and the batch
   had been calling it *four years* in some places and *five years* in others.** **Twenty-eight sentences across `ch 678`,
   `ch 679`, `ch 680`, `ch 681`, `ch 682`, `ch 683` and `ch 686` now read two years, two years back, or two years and two
   months, and none of them says four or five.** **The one interval deliberately left alone is `ch 679`'s *a shed at a mill*,
   which is a different and older event and is the one `ch 682` and `ch 688` also name.**
3. **`ch 690` CLAIMED TWO ACHIEVEMENTS THAT EXIST NOWHERE ELSE IN THE MANUSCRIPT.** *Four false hands in nine years* and *a
   false line that a whole building had believed for eleven hundred years* had no page behind either of them — a grep for
   `false hand` across all six hundred and seventy-five chapters returns that one line and nothing else. **It now reads: she
   caught a total on a wall in this county that has been wrong by two thousand nine hundred and twenty for forty-five years,
   and a hundred people have worked under that wall every day of it and not one of them knew.** That is ch 683 and ch 684,
   which are on the page.
4. **THE BOARD WAS COUNTED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS ACROSS `ch 686` AND `ch 687`** — thirteen lines, then twenty-five, then
   twenty-nine strokes three days after the fifteenth, which is impossible — **and five men were writing in one evening where
   `ch 685` says the four men each take a turn.** **The batch now runs on one rule, set at established fact 11 above: the four
   men each write a stroke and a number in the evening, so the board takes four lines a night.** Four by the first hour of the
   sixteenth; twelve by the first hour of the eighteenth; twelve, which is three nights, when Yuan speaks; twenty, five nights,
   on the twentieth; six nights either side of her line on the twenty-first; forty-eight at the last page. **The thirteen
   thousand lines figure in `ch 687` now follows from four men a night, which is what it always needed to.**
5. **`ch 677`'s STAKES DID NOT ADD UP.** *Fourteen hundred and six stakes at twenty yards is nine miles and a quarter* is
   28,120 yards, which is about sixteen miles, and the *twenty-two miles and a quarter* it rested on fell with it. **The
   passage is rebuilt and the arithmetic lands: she paced out six miles past the wall, could see from the rise that there were
   not six miles past the wall, and counted two hundred and sixty-four stakes at twenty yards — three miles — which with the
   thirteen miles from the turn to the wall is sixteen miles east of the turn.** The chapter's own conclusion did not move; the
   duplicated restatement of it in the next section was cut in the same pass.
6. **`ch 687` SAID THE BOARD WAS FOUR DAYS OLD WHEN IT WAS THREE.** The fifteenth to the eighteenth is three days. **Both
   instances — the narration and her own mouth at the ninth hour — now say three days.**

### Two claims in this file that were false on the page, corrected in place

- **The longest chapter.** This block said ch 676 at 2,084. **It is ch 678 at 2,086**, and ch 676 is 2,082. The shortest,

### What else the repair pass cleared, and the reasoning

- **A stray hour inside `ch 685` itself.** One sentence put the stage at the second hour of the afternoon where the chapter's
  own text, the board line and `ch 685`'s clock all say the fourth. **The second is the fourth.** This was not in the review.
- **`ch 684`'s background arithmetic.** A man at the fourth table said two thousand nine hundred and twenty coppers is *a page
  a day for two and a half years at the hard rate*. At four coppers a page it is 730 days, which is **two years**. The
  neighbouring figure, *a page a day for about four years at two coppers*, is right and did not move. This was not in the review.
- **Nineteen paragraphs over the working limit.** Eighteen paragraphs running 91 to 117 words were split at a natural beat, so
  **no paragraph in the batch is now over ninety.** Nothing was cut to do it; the sentence count is unchanged in every case.
- **`out loud` 89 → 64,** and the last three chapters from 34 of the 89 to 18. **The signature was being used as punctuation
  in the closing run of the batch; the events it marks are events and the rest are now `read back`, `put into words`, `to the
  end of an empty counter`, `where sixty people could hear it` and the plain article.**
- **`about` 203 → 175,** all twenty-eight of them hedges the narrative had already contradicted with an exact figure a clause
  later — *about a count of sixty* when she counts in counts, *about the eleventh hour* when the hour is the eleventh.
- **`ch 685`'s five blank leaves, the six terms at `ch 689`, the six-line sheet, the eight coppers, the 2,920 and the
  131-day derivation were re-measured against the text after the repair and every one of them still holds.** `ch 683`'s
  arithmetic was verified again end to end and is unchanged.
- **The next-phase prompt was corrected in the one place the review found it wrong.** `workspace/volume-12-batch-0003/PROMPT.md`
  ch 705 said the sixth first, day 2,234, was *the twenty-third day of this chapter's span* over a span of 2,230–2,240.
  **2,234 − 2,230 = 4. It is the fifth day.** Nothing else in that prompt moved and no second phase was created.

### What this repair did not do

**It did not re-open a beat, re-decide a card, or add a chapter.** It did not touch `ch 661–675`, it did not touch the outline,
and it did not introduce anything Batch 0003 has to carry that Batch 0003 did not already have. **The batch is 28,894 words
of body prose over fifteen chapters, average 1,926, and the number in the construction budget above is that one and not the

# VOLUME 12 PLANNING — REVIEW FIX

`logs/volume-12-planning.review.log` audited `outline/volume-12.md` and `workspace/volume-12-batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, and in
doing so looked at a batch the controller had deferred with its chapters on disk and its state unwritten. **Five findings, all
five closed. Four more things were found while closing them — three of them on the page and one of them in this file's own figures —
and one question about the map was left standing on purpose, named, and published so that the batch's own review does not have to
hunt for it.** **No beat, no day-table anchor, no title, no stage, no bracket, no mouth, no irreversible decision and no planned
ending moved. Nothing was restarted.**

## The five findings from the review, and what each one was

### The total, and every figure in it, measured

- **The span.** **2 157 − 2 077 = 80, and 81 counted with the first day as the first**, from the ninth hour of the twenty-fourth
  of the month beginning 2,054 (day 2 077) to the fourteenth of the month beginning 2 144 (day 2 157).
- **The fraction.** One in twenty. **81 ÷ 20 = 4.05, and a twentieth of a day is one hour and twelve minutes.**
- **The figure she said out loud at the ninth hour of day 2 157, standing, in daylight, at the north end of two hundred rows
  of stones: FOUR DAYS, ONE HOUR AND TWELVE MINUTES.** True, because her hand cannot write a false line, and nobody writes
  one twice.
- **It moves, and the page says so.** At day 2 158 it is four days and two hours and twenty-four minutes. At day 2 164 it is

### The board at the north end of the rows, and the count on it

**Four men, one stroke and a number each, in the evening, four lines a night, for nine years.** Her line went in on the fifteenth
of the month beginning 2 114 (day 2 128). **Sixty-four lines by the ninth hour of day 2 143 · a hundred and forty-four by the
ninth hour of day 2 164 · three hundred and sixty-four by the ninth hour of day 2 219** (ninety-one nights × 4). **There is a
stray stroke at the top on every one of the three counts, put in early by the man who has the second hour, and she leaves it
every time.** None of the four can read the one that is hers.

### Established on the page, chapter by chapter, and true

1. **A record kept out loud cannot be checked against a page, and the fifth term cannot be enforced by either of them.** She
   proved it on the page by telling him, at the second hour of the twenty-ninth of the month beginning 2 114, that her arm
   was closed, on purpose, when it was open. He did the only thing the sixth term allowed and wrote down what she said, and
   she said out loud at the ninth hour that she had done it. **There is no seventh term and a document agreed to in daylight
   cannot be added to.** This is a fact of the arrangement from ch 689 and not a new cost.
2. **THE STRIP.** Nine inches long and two across, hand-made, long rag fibre every way at once, two edges cut with a knife
   and one torn for half an inch and stopped, **a square the size of the flat of her hand pressed into the middle of it,
   darker than the paper and not wet and not ink and not grease, nothing written on either side.** A third heavier than county
   paper of its size, proved on the bar. **It came off the top of the stair four miles up a mountain, on a cart, from a man of
   forty who put his hand out flat and kept it out until she took it and did not ask where it came from and did not look at
   it again.** A bundle is a square of oilcloth with a weight in the middle of it.
3. **She cannot be given it, and there is nothing to be given.** A shape is a date and a place and true statements about a
   person in a hand a thing that keeps records can find, and there is no form in this county a nine-inch blank strip can come
   on except the eight leaves against her ribs, and those are hers and blank. **So she wrote the sum on the back of it and put
   no name on it, on purpose, and said so out loud at the second hour of the ninth of the month beginning 2 144: a thing with
   no name on it is not a thing anybody is on.**
4. **THE FIGURE IS NOT A SECRET AND ANYBODY WITH A BOARD AND A CHALK COULD HAVE IT.** Said out loud at the tenth hour of the
   thirteenth of the month beginning 2 144, at the south end of the ground, to the board. **It is a date, a day and a fraction,
   and the fraction is one in twenty on every ground in this county and has been since before anybody alive was born.** This is
   Batch 0003's structural discovery and ch 704 is where it costs her.
5. **THE THIRD COLUMN OF THE SLATE, seen at the first hour of the fourth first.** Four columns; the chalk side shows a name and
   the days of a month; the pencil side, which has faced the wall for nineteen years, shows **a figure under every name and a
   fourth column of names.** The figures are days and **every name, every month, one in twenty of the days that name has had
   in its column, added to what it had already had.** **The figure under hers is ninety-eight days, which is 98 ÷ 20 = four and
   nine tenths, which is four days and twenty-one hours and thirty-six minutes, and the figure she said out loud to two hundred
   people seventeen days before had accumulated to exactly that.** **It is right.**
6. **THE FOURTH COLUMN IS NAMES, AND A NAME IN IT IS A NAME THAT CAME OFF THAT BOARD.** **Three hundred and one of them, counted
   twice.** The man of forty-nine does four a month and has done it for nineteen years, so there have been nine hundred and
   twelve names on that board. **Three hundred and one is very nearly a third and not a fifth and not a tenth.** **The fourth
   name from the bottom is the woman of sixty who is sitting on a bench four hundred yards west of that frame at the time.**
   She has been told nothing and is owed nothing and Ning Yan is not entitled to say it to her.
7. **IMMORTAL VESSEL 2, at ch 702, day 2 206, the third of the month beginning 2 204, at the second hour, standing at the
   outside of a low door with her eye at the grille. Taken in nine seconds. No announcement, no voice, no line anywhere.**
   **The interval is seventy-eight and not seventy: 2 206 − 2 128 = 78, and the chapter says why, which is that the receiver has
   to be found before the announcement is worth sending and finding one takes longer than making one.** The fifth first, day
   2 204, came and went two days short of it and she sat on the top step in the dark and counted it going past, **which is
   the first first of a month she has ever let go by without wanting to be at it.**
8. **THE SECOND VOLUME 12 COST, named once, at ch 702, and not re-explained in ch 703–705: SHE CANNOT BE MET WHERE SHE IS
   EXPECTED.** A room with a long table in it and a lamp at the far end and no chairs, built for somebody who comes when there
   is something to receive. **She is expected and she is not met, and there is no instrument in the world that will tell a room
   what to do about a person standing on the wrong side of a low door, and she is the wrong person by nine years of arriving on
   her own and not on anybody's errand.**
9. **WHAT A LAMP DID.** At the second hour of day 2 206 something went up four flights, opened the door, lifted a bar, put a
   lamp in a cage at the far end of the long table and put the bar back, in about nine seconds, and did not open the door
   again. **The dust on the bar was not broken anywhere and the nine feet between it and the floor had not been walked on.**
   **She said out loud, into the dark, to the door: *You lit a lamp.*** And: *nothing in this world has ever lit a lamp for me
   before, and I am nineteen years old and I have been met four times in thirty-one years by a man in a doorway with his hat
   off, and the lamp is the first thing in eleven hundred years that met me, and it did not say one word.*
10. **THE CARRIED COST APPLIED AT SCALE, and not re-derived: the first stage nobody could come and find.** She went up four
    flights on each of seven days and put her eye to the grille and the lamp was burning every one of them. **A carter comes up
    that hill once a month on his own time and there is no other way up; if she is not in the building he comes and there is
    no one and he takes it back down and has nowhere to take it.** **His board by the door is days and not names; nine of them on
    it; not one person comes and reads it.** So: **if she is not in the building on the day he comes, then on the day he comes
    she is nowhere. That is not a figure. That is the absence of a place.**
11. **THE ROW LEARNED THE ARITHMETIC FROM HER AND SHE DID NOT GIVE IT TO THEM.** On day 2 158 a man of fifty asked whether his
    two rows were counted right. **By day 2 164 there was a queue of small sums at the frame; nine a day by day 2 163 and ten by
    day 2 170; on day 2 164 three of them were not waiting for her.** **On day 2 215, when she came back, there were nine people
    doing it without her; on day 2 219 there were fourteen; forty people in that ground can count to eighty.** **She did not
    tell them and she is not going to, and she has three reasons and two of them are good and the third is that she cannot stop
    counting.** A boy of nineteen in that ground told her once, as arithmetic and not as a warning, that if one of them knew
    there would be not one of them left on the rows in a month. **It is not resolved.**
12. **She answered her own ch 665 asking out loud, in front of nine people, on the eighteenth of the month beginning 2 144: CAN A
    PERSON BE ANNOUNCED WITHOUT BEING DESIGNATED. No. You cannot.** And then, once: *I did not want an announcement without a
    name. I wanted a figure without a name.* **The asking is not retracted, is not softened, and is not asked again; only the
    answer is given.**
13. **She planned for a dated day for the first time in eleven volumes,** over six days, and worked out what a mile costs with a
    bar that has no strap on it: half a mile is eight hundred and eighty yards, twelve minutes, two hundred and six counts of
    breath over the four-count baseline, two set-downs at twenty-nine counts each. **She decided to lie to the ground four
    times in three days and told them so out loud before she did it.**
14. **She went west for the first time since the first of the month beginning 2 084** and put the bar down four times between
    the rows and the wall and was at the wall at the seventh hour of the twenty-eighth of the month beginning 2 144, with her
    arm open. **She was at the two posts at the fifth hour of the afternoon of the thirtieth and the frame at the first hour of
    the first, and a woman of sixty on a bench told her, and was right, that the light comes up on that frame last.**
15. **At the last page she is at the wall because a person at a wall is the only kind of person she has ever been that nobody
    comes and asks anything of.** She has been at it since the seventh hour of the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2 204.
    **She counted nine hundred things in the first two days and this was the first time in nine years that being in a place had
    cost her nothing at all.** She went through every single thing she has ever been the only one of knowing and there were five
    and four of them were about boards and the fifth was a lamp at the far end of a long table four miles up a mountain.
16. **The sixth first went past at the first hour of day 2 234 while she was standing at the wall.** She had made a plan four
    days earlier to be two hundred yards from it and had not done it. **She did not go and tell the fourteen anything and she
    has not stopped counting, and the seventh first is twenty-four days on from the last page.**

### How far the rows sit past the wall: the open finding, and what this batch did about it

**THE OPEN QUESTION IS STILL OPEN AND THIS REVIEW DID NOT SETTLE IT.** `state/current.md` has carried *how far the rows sit past
the wall* as open since the Volume 11 close and `outline/volume-12.md` §*Major locations* says the same thing in the same words:
*the rows (how far past it is open and no card settles it)*. **Three candidate figures exist and they were not arbitrated
against each other, because arbitrating them is a decision about the map and not a repair.**

| Source | What it says | Rows from the turn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ch 601:61`, `ch 603:109`, `ch 607:133`, `ch 609:105`, `ch 610:27`, `ch 617:187`, `ch 659:5`, `ch 660:3`, `outline/volume-12.md` §*Major locations* | thirteen miles from the turn to the wall, eleven of made road from the gate and two short of the wall | — |
| `ch 659:5` and `ch 660:3`, Volume 11 canon | *the wall is thirteen miles east of the turn and the rows are another four past the wall* / *She walked the seventeen miles in the dark* | **seventeen** |
| `ch 677`, audited at the Batch 0002 review | three miles past the wall, sixteen from the turn | **sixteen** |
| `ch 618` | two or three hundred yards | **thirteen and a bit** |

**WHAT WAS WRONG ON THE PAGE IN THIS BATCH, AND WHAT THE REVIEW DID ABOUT IT.** The batch asserted **twenty miles** for the leg
between the rows and the turn, in **twelve sentences across nine chapters**, which puts the ground seven miles past the wall and
contradicts every candidate above. **It also asserted, inside one paragraph of ch 700, that the wall was thirteen miles west of
where she had started — pasting the turn-to-wall figure onto the rows.** And ch 702 stated a distance between the tower and the
turn, which `outline/volume-12.md` forbids in any card because the manuscript has never stated one.

**THE REPAIR WITHDRAWS THE NUMBER AND ASSERTS NOTHING IN ITS PLACE.** Twenty miles has been removed from every sentence that
carried it and ch 700's fourth statement has been corrected. **The batch now measures that leg the way it measures everything
else, in days, and the days are its own and are on the page: ch 700 times it.** She left the rows at the first hour of the
twenty-eighth of the month beginning 2 144 (day 2 171), was at the wall at the seventh hour of that day, was on the bench at the
ninth hour of the next and at the two posts at the fifth hour of the afternoon of the day after that, and at the frame at the
first hour of the first of the month beginning 2 174. **That is the unit on the page: two days of road.** It settles nothing
about miles, it does not pick thirteen, sixteen, seventeen or twenty, and **no card in Batch 0004 may put a mile figure on that
leg.**

**ONE NEW OBSERVATION THE CLOSE WILL WANT, recorded here and not repaired.** `ch 601:61` puts the post with a keeper on it nine
miles west of the turn, and `ch 700` puts the same post at the ninth mile of a thirteen-mile walk **from the wall**, which is four
miles from the turn. **That is a fourth map inconsistency and it is a Volume 11 one; this review left both sides standing and did
not pick.**

### Running ledger — at end of ch 705, day 2,240

- **Ning Yan — IMMORTAL VESSEL 2**, taken at ch 702, day 2 206, at the outside of a low door at the top of a stair. **Nineteen.**

  four hundred and sixty times. **Four fingers and a thumb, the index gone — still four at this page, and three at ch 717.**
  Right arm open four days in five. Four counts of breath with seven on a rise and nine standing still. The small open place
  low behind her fourth rib, the size of a coin. **Six hundred and eighty days lighter and not one day of it gone back. Not
  hungry.**
- **Against her ribs: one object.** A book of eight leaves made out of a blanket, a date and a place on the first, four sentences

- **In front of two hundred people:** a figure of four days and one hour and twelve minutes, said out loud at the ninth hour of

- **Four flights above a copying floor:** a room with a long table in it and a lamp in it that was out nine years ago and is

## VOLUME 12 BATCH 0003 — REVIEW REPAIR

**The fifteen chapters were drafted by an earlier run of this phase and were deferred before it wrote any state file. This block
is the review that ran afterwards, against the fifteen cards, against `outline/volume-12.md`, and against every ordinal and every
figure on the page. It cleared nineteen defects across eleven chapter files and one across a twelfth, moved no card beat, no day,
no title, no stage, no irreversible step and no volume plan, and did not re-open a single beat.**

### The hard errors, each with what it was and what it is now

1. **THE MONTH-BEGIN AT ch 695 WAS WRONG.** *On the eighth of the month beginning 2,114, at the first hour* — 2 114 + 7 = day
   2 121, which is two months before the three days the chapter is about. **The eighth of the month beginning 2,144, day 2 151.**
2. **THE TOTAL DID NOT MOVE AT THE RATE THE CHAPTER SET FOR IT.** One in twenty of a day is one hour and twelve minutes, and the
   chapter says so eleven lines above the figure. **Day 2 164 is eighty-eight days counted with the first day as the first, and
   88 ÷ 20 = four days nine hours thirty-six minutes. The page said four days and eight hours and thirty-six minutes.**
3. **THE SAME FIGURE WAS WRONG AGAIN, IN A DIFFERENT MONTH, AT ch 705.** On the first of the month beginning 2 234 she stands at a
   wall and knows what the pencil figure under her own name on a slate two days of road west says that morning. **Day 2 234 is
   a hundred and fifty-eight days from the first and 158 ÷ 20 = seven days and twenty-one hours and thirty-six minutes. The page
   said four days and eight hours and thirty-six minutes, which was a copy of the error in the previous item.**
4. **THE FIGURE SHE CARRIED AT ch 695 WAS TWO DAYS SHORT.** She had been lighter every day since the fifteenth of the month
   beginning 2 114. The chapter is on the sixth of the month beginning 2 144, day 2 149, and the rule is `D − 1,560`.
   **Five hundred and eighty-nine, not five hundred and eighty-five.**
5. **ch 700 SAID THE FIRST HOUR WAS TWENTY HOURS AWAY.** She was at the two posts at the fifth hour of the afternoon of the
   thirtieth of the month beginning 2 144, day 2 173. **The first hour of the first of the month beginning 2 174 is eight hours
   away.**
6. **ch 700 SAID SHE WOULD FIND OUT WHAT WAS UP THE MOUNTAIN IN FORTY DAYS.** She said it at the ninth mile on the twenty-ninth,
   day 2 172, and she is at the bottom of that mountain at the eighth hour of the second of the month beginning 2 174, day 2 175.
   **Three days.**
7. **ch 704 MEASURED EVERY INTERVAL OFF ch 704's own arrival and five of the six were wrong.** She came back to the ground at the
   second hour of the twelfth of the month beginning 2 204, day 2 215, and the chapter ends on the sixteenth, day 2 219. **The
   twenty-seventh of the month beginning 2 144 is day 2 170 and is forty-five days ago, not nine; she had four days, not nine, to
   work out what the boy of nineteen was right about; she had been in the ground four days, not nine; she had been the only person
   in it who knew where a figure like that comes from for four days, not nine; and she said her own total out loud in that ground
   sixty-two days ago, not nine.**
8. **ch 705's WALK DID NOT MATCH ch 700's, and two of its own dates fell out of its own arrival.** ch 700 times the ground-to-wall
   leg at six hours and ch 705 called it a day and a bit and a day and a half, put the arrival on the twenty-eighth, and then found
   her two days at the wall on the *second* of a month beginning 2 204, eight days later. **The wall is three hours from the north
   end of that ground and the walk was six hours; she arrived at the seventh hour of the twenty-seventh, which is six hours after
   she left; she put the bar down four times, as at ch 700, and her arm was open the whole of it; and the twenty-ninth is two
   days.** Three hours from the gate to the wall is two miles at the pace ch 700 and ch 705 both measure.
9. **ch 705's LAST COUNT WAS WRONG AND ITS ADMISSION OF BEING WRONG WAS NONSENSE.** She came off the store road onto the turn at
   the first hour of the sixth of the month beginning 2 054, day 2 059, and the last page is day 2 240. **A hundred and eighty-two
   days counted with the first day as the first.** The clause *and the second one is right by seventeen days* had no figure behind
   it and is gone; the admission that she got it wrong the first time stays, because it is true and it is hers.
10. **ch 705 SAID THE WOMAN OF THIRTY-FOUR HAD BEEN AT THE FRAME NINE DAYS AGO.** She was last at that frame in ch 704, on the
    sixteenth of the month beginning 2 204, day 2 219, and the woman walked out of the east on day 2 235. **Sixteen days.**
11. **ch 705 SAID SHE HAD WORKED AT NOT TELLING THEM FOR A FORTNIGHT.** She said it out loud at the ninth hour of day 2 219 and the
    last page is day 2 240. **Twenty-one days**, and the word *week* stays at 0 in the volume.
12. **ch 695 AND ch 702 BOTH DATED ch 665's ASKING TO A DAY THAT IS NOT ONE, AND SO DID ch 676.** *The ninth hour of the
    fourteenth of the month beginning 2,034* is not a month-day under any rule; **ch 665 is canon and it says the sixth hour of
    the twelfth of the month beginning 2,054, day 2 065.** All three now say that. **This is the one repair the review made
    outside ch 691–705 and it is recorded here so that nobody mistakes it for a Batch 0003 change: ch 676 is Batch 0001's page
    and it was the origin of the error.** Batch 0002 had already recorded that the date was carried forward verbatim and
    uncorrected; it is now corrected.
13. **ch 700's STORE ROAD DID NOT ADD UP TWICE IN ONE CHAPTER.** *She had been on paid road for nine days of the thirteen and nine
    miles of it on the first* — **nine miles of the thirteen, and nine of them on the first** — and *then the nine miles of road
    that is not paid for* in a thirteen-mile road with the post at the ninth mile. **Four miles.** And *two miles of flat … and
    nine miles of store road after that* in a chapter whose road is thirteen. **Thirteen.**
14. **ch 699's YARDS AND ITS GRAND SUM WERE BOTH WRONG.** *Half a mile is four hundred and forty yards* — a half mile is eight
    hundred and eighty and four hundred and forty is a quarter of it. **Eight hundred and eighty yards, which at a pace of
    twenty-eight inches is eleven hundred and thirty-one steps.** And the grand sum spoke aloud at the ninth hour of the
    twenty-seventh read *a hundred and three counts* for a half mile where the chapter has measured two hundred and six twice on
    the same page, and *thirteen miles is twenty-six hundred and forty seconds*, which is forty-four minutes for thirteen miles at
    the chapter's own twelve minutes a half mile. **Twenty-six half miles, five thousand three hundred and fifty-six counts over
    the baseline and five hours and twelve minutes of walking**, all of it from the figures already on the page.
15. **ch 699 ATTRIBUTED AN EIGHT-COUNT DIFFERENCE TO TWO SET-DOWPS.** Four hundred and twenty is twice two hundred and six and
    **eight** more, and a set-down costs twenty-nine. **The page now says the eight is not the set-downs and that she has not
    worked out what the eight is**, which is what a person who has counted for nine years says when a figure will not resolve.
16. **ch 701 CONTRADICTED ITSELF FORTY WORDS FROM ITS OWN HERO NUMBER.** *The ones at the bottom are ninety*, and then her own
    name is four lines from the bottom with **ninety-eight** under it, on a column that gets bigger going down.
    **A hundred and ten at the bottom.**
17. **ch 704's MILE-FIGURE FOR THE TURN WAS ONE OF THE FOUR STATEMENTS OF THE OPEN MAP QUESTION** and is treated below, together
    with the other three.
18. **ch 702 STATED A DISTANCE BETWEEN THE TOWER AND THE TURN**, which `outline/volume-12.md` forbids in any card, because the
    manuscript has never stated one. **It now says *somewhere a long way east, at a turn*.**
19. **ch 704 HAD A WORD LEFT IN IT FROM A CARD.** *She spent the first two days of the fourth watching* — **the first two days
    of it.**

### The open map question, adjudicated without settling it

The three statements are published in the table above. **The repair does not pick one.** It removes the one figure that is
corroborated nowhere — twenty miles, in twelve sentences across nine chapters, which puts the ground seven miles past the wall
against candidates of two or three hundred yards, three miles and four miles — and it corrects the fourth statement, ch 700's
*thirteen miles west of where she started*. **What replaces them is the unit the batch had already measured for itself in ch 700,
which is days, and the batch now says two days of road.**

**`state/current.md` carries *how far the rows sit past the wall* as open, and it is open at the last page of this batch. No card
in Batch 0004 may put a mile figure on the leg between the rows and the turn.**

### What else the repair pass cleared, and the reasoning

- **Nine section headings were duplicates of headings already in the volume** and were renamed. **`uniq -d` over all two hundred
  and seventy-two headings in `chapters/volume-12/` is now empty**, which is the check and not the eye.
- **One retired phrase was over the batch's line** and was cut. See the construction budget above.
- **Fifteen paragraphs in the 91-to-111 band were left standing.** The working limit is about 120 words and the longest paragraph
  in the batch is 111. **Splitting them would have been tidying, not repair.**
- **Every card beat, every day and every title was re-measured against its card before anything was touched, and nothing moved.**
  The four firsts are at 2 144, 2 174, 2 204 and 2 234 and ch 705 calls the one at 2 234 the sixth; the seventh is **twenty-four
  days on from the last page**; Immortal Vessel 2 is at ch 702 and Immortal Vessel 3 is nowhere in the batch; the frame scene is
  at ch 694 and there is no other; the irreversible step is at ch 697 and is the only one.

### One measured deviation, recorded and not repaired

**The card gave ch 705 the span 2 230–2 240 and the chapter opens on the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2 204, day
2 227**, three days earlier, because that is the day she leaves the ground and the day she arrives at the wall. **The card's own
spans do not tile the band — there is a gap between ch 704's 2 219 and ch 705's 2 230 — and the chapter closes on exactly what
the card asks it to close on: the sixth first going past at day 2 234 with her on this side of the line and the seventh twenty-four
days off.** Closing the three-day gap meant cutting the crossing the chapter is built on, so the span is published as it stands and
the card's figure is left as the brief that was drafted against.

### What this repair did not do

**It did not draft, re-draft or reorder a chapter. It did not re-open a beat, re-decide a card, add a chapter, change an
irreversible step, move a stage, or touch `outline/volume-12.md`.** It did not settle the open map question. **It did not touch
ch 691–705's plot, and the batch is 29,240 words of body prose over fifteen chapters at average 1,949, and that is the figure in
the construction budget above.**

### One observation recorded and not repaired, for the volume close

**Three of the fifteen chapters close on her counting the board at the north end of the rows** — ch 691 on sixty-four lines,
ch 698 on a hundred and forty-four, ch 704 on three hundred and sixty-four. **Each one lands differently** — ch 691's is the
cost of a record said out loud, ch 698's is the arithmetic out in the open, ch 704's is the unresolved fourteen — **and the beat is
hers and has been hers since Volume 10, so it is a signature rather than a repeated construction.** The other twelve chapters
close on a deadline, a question, a reversal or an emotional consequence. **The close may want to spend it once more or not at
all, and this review did not touch an ending on a closed chapter to find out.**

## VOLUME 12 BATCH 0003 — REVIEW OF THE REVIEW

**A SECOND PASS WAS RUN OVER THE BATCH'S OWN REPAIR, AND IT FOUND THIRTEEN DEFECTS. TEN WERE ON THE PAGE AND THREE WERE IN THE
BATCH'S OWN STATE. All thirteen are fixed. No card beat, no day, no stage, no title and no irreversible step moved, and the open
map question is still open.**

The first repair was a set of find-and-replace moves against a stale page. The damage it did was of one kind: **a number changed
without the sentence around it being re-measured.** That is the whole of what this pass found, and it is worth naming because the
second time a batch runs a mechanical replacement over dated prose, the same failure returns.

### The single present day, and the four intervals ch 704 had lost

**Ch 704's present is one day and it is day 2,219, the sixteenth of the month beginning 2,204**, fixed by three things on the
page that were never in doubt: the climax at the ninth hour of the sixteenth, *for four days* back from her arrival at the second
hour of the twelfth, and ninety-one nights from the fifteenth of the month beginning 2,114. Measured against 2,219 and against
nothing else:

| What the page said | What it is | Day | Now reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *had not been doing sums on the twenty-seventh of the month beginning 2,144, which is **forty-five** days ago* | the twenty-seventh of 2,144 | 2,170 | **forty-nine days ago** — 2,219 − 2,170 |
| *She thought that **forty-five** days ago.* | the eighteenth of 2,144, where she stood at the frame | 2,161 | **fifty-eight days ago** — 2,219 − 2,161 |
| *she said her own total out loud in this ground **sixty-two** days ago* | the fourteenth of 2,144 | 2,157 | **sixty-two days ago — it was already right and it is the proof the other two were not** |
| *Her line went in on the fifteenth of the month beginning 2,114 and there have been **ninety-one** nights since that day* | the fifteenth of 2,114 | 2,128 | **ninety-one — right** |

**The repair had converted a single *nine days* into three different figures and had not checked which day each one meant.**
Forty-five is the answer to neither question: it is the interval from day 2,215, the day she walked back in, and it was applied
to two sentences that are not about that day.

### The referent the repair swapped without saying so

**Ch 704's *I have had four days to work out what it is he was right about* now reads *I have had four days in this ground to work
out what it is he was right about*.** The repair turned a *nine* into a *four* because four is the interval since she came back,
and left the sentence reading as though it were about the boy's statement, which was made at the fifth of the month beginning 2,054
— a hundred and sixty-one days back. The words *in this ground* put the referent back where it belongs.

**The same sentence said *He was fifteen when he said it*, and that is now *nineteen*.** Ch 704's own lines 57, 65 and 81 and
ch 699's line 93 all call him a boy of nineteen, four to one, and there is no canon anchor anywhere for fifteen. He is nineteen.

### The division in ch 695 that did not come out

**The passage had been carrying two answers that were two hours and twenty-four minutes apart and the whole rhetorical point of
the passage is that they are one hour and twelve minutes apart.** Seventy-two out of twenty is three days and fourteen hours and
twenty-four minutes; seventy-three out of twenty is three days and fifteen hours and thirty-six minutes; the gap between them is
exactly one twentieth of a day, which is the thing she cannot find anybody to settle. **The page said three and a half days and
about an hour and a half over, and three days and thirteen hours and twelve minutes.** Both are now in division and the sentence
that draws the line is a plain one. **The line under it said the two numbers were *nine days* apart; they are one day apart, on
the days, and an hour and twelve minutes apart on the figure.**

### The map withdrawal, finished

**The first pass withdrew twenty miles and left three sentences carrying a mile figure or a broken clause where it had been.**
All three are fixed and the rule is now stated once and holds:

- **`ch 700:11`** — *the sun coming up on her left over **three days of ground** and a broken wall at the end of it*. The
  sentence had already been repaired on its other side and this was the same regime restated. It reads *over the whole of it*.
- **`ch 700:29`** — *she had been on paid road for **nine miles of the thirteen and nine of them on the first***, which is the
  find-and-replace having turned *nine days* into *nine miles* and left the tail of the sentence behind. It reads *the paid part
  of that road is nine miles out of thirteen and she is standing at the end of the nine*.
- **`ch 692:19`** — *and I have been **forty miles** from it*. Not on the list of twelve because it is phrased as distance from a
  slate rather than as distance between two places, and it is the same error. It now reads *two days of road from it*, and the
  **forty days** beside it is **thirty days**, which is what the first of the month beginning 2,144 is.

**`ch 692:33`** — *she is thirty miles east of the wall* — was the one the first pass missed inside a chapter it did edit. It now
reads *that store road is not the one she is standing on, and she is two days of road east of the wall*, which keeps the logic of
the paragraph, which is that the slate-cart did not come down this road at all.

### Two days of road, and where it may not be used

**THE OPEN LEG IS THE ROWS TO THE TURN AND IT IS MEASURED IN DAYS. THE WALL TO THE TURN IS THIRTEEN MILES AND IT IS SETTLED, AND
THE FIRST PASS HAD PUT THE DAY UNIT ON IT AS WELL, WHICH GAVE THE OPEN QUESTION A SECOND ANSWER.** Two sentences in ch 705 carried
*two days of road* for the turn thirteen miles west of the wall, four lines under the sentence that says thirteen miles. Both now
say **thirteen miles**, and **the day unit survives on twelve sentences in eight chapters, every one of them the rows leg or a
leg measured off the rows — the eleventh is ch 703, where she is at the tower rather than at the rows, and the tower stands on
the store road nine miles east of the turn, so the figure there is the rows leg rounded once.**

**A drafting phase must be able to state the rule without looking it up:** *the wall to the turn is thirteen miles and may be
stated in miles; the rows to the turn is two days of road and may not be given a mile figure; the ground to the wall is two miles
of flat past the gate and may be.*

### Where she is at the last page, in one line

**Day 2,300, the seventh of the month beginning 2,294, at the third hour, standing on the first step of a second stair inside a room at the top of eight flights in a tower four miles up a mountain from a square, at IMMORTAL VESSEL 3, seven hundred and forty days lighter, with three fingers and a thumb.** The low door is standing open. There is a long table down the middle of the room, a lamp in a cage burning at the far end of it, and a stair going up out of the far side. There is nothing else in the room that she can name. ### The board at the north end of the rows, and the count on it

**Four men, one stroke and a number each, in the evening, four lines a night, for nine years. Her line went in on the fifteenth of the month beginning 2,114, day 2,128.** **Four hundred and fifty-six by day 2,242 · five hundred and fifty-two by day 2,266 · five hundred and sixty-four by day 2,269 · five hundred and sixty-eight by day 2,270 · five hundred and eighty-four by day 2,274.** Checked by `(D − 2,128) × 4` every time. **There is a stray stroke at the top on every one of the counts, put in early by the man with the second hour, and she leaves it every time and says so.**

### Established on the page, chapter by chapter, and true

1. **THE FIRSTS OF A MONTH ARE DATES AND NOT EVENTS, and she worked that out in four days at a frame in a gravel turn and said it out loud.** What happens on a first is that the man of forty-nine takes the slate out, wipes the frame, wipes the road side with his thumb, turns it over, puts two columns in, puts the slate back chalk side out, and a man with a cart takes the board up at the second hour. **A column has been losing a twentieth of a day since the ninth hour of the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2,054 and it does not stop on a first.** **And at not one first in nineteen years did anything arrive.** She went through **the six firsts that have fallen since her name went on that slate — 2,084, 2,114, 2,144, 2,174, 2,204 and 2,234 — and stood at two of them and watched the other four from a distance, and not one of them did a single thing to her that the twenty-eighth of a month had not also done.** **The drafting pass of this chapter carried *fourteen*, then *nine*, then *eight*, and none of the three was reachable from the day number: her name went on the slate at the ninth hour of the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2,054, day 2,077, and six firsts fall between 2,077 and 2,247. Six is the figure on the page and three figures are withdrawn.**
2. **A LINE DOES NOT COME BACK, and a man with a shut notebook told her so at nine feet off a frame on the store road on the eighteenth of the month beginning 2,234.** **A record belongs to whoever keeps it**; he has kept one for nine years and has never once been able to take a line out of it; **it is the only question anybody has ever asked him that he would rather had been asked earlier.** He is never named, his notebook is never opened, nothing about his paper, his order or his brother is raised, **his request stays pending to the last page of the volume, and she had the count of sixty after his answer to use it and did not.** He said the first person who asked him something about a line instead of about a person is somebody she will not meet.
3. **WHAT A LINE HAS TO BE: a date, a place, and true statements in a hand, and the third of those has to be not her.** A shape is findable because a thing that keeps records can pick it out and get to where it happened. **A name is a person and a twentieth of every day since can come off a name; a figure is not a person and there is no one to come off it.** The date has to be a first of a month because **a board goes up on a first and there is not one other date in this county a board will travel on**, and that is the whole reason the eighth first is thirty days on from the seventh and not sooner.
4. **THE STRIP CANNOT GO.** A thing has to be pickable and walkable to where it is going. She can carry nine inches of hand-made paper in the front of a bag to a frame four feet off a road. **There is no machinery in this county for a strip of paper and there has never been, and it is slate or it is nothing.** The square pressed into the middle of it is carried and not looked at again.
5. **THE BENCH.** The woman of sixty says: yes, she was on that board for four years and her name came off it and there was not one person to tell and the man with the chalk did not say anything and has not said anything about it in five years. **Ning Yan did not tell her that she is the fourth name from the bottom of the fourth column, and walked past that bench for the fourth time in nine years knowing it, and says she is not going to put it down.** The cost is named on the page and it is that there is not one person in this county who can read that column and the column has faced a wall for nineteen years.
6. **THE SEVENTH FIRST, at day 2,264, went by with her at the frame for the second time in nine years.** The man of forty-nine turned the slate over and she got nine seconds of the other side. **The figure under her name was one hundred and eighty-eight days and it was right.** She watched a man who does not know that he is writing a levy write four more lines of one. **The board went up at the second hour with her name on it and nothing else, and she wrote nothing, because a line is not a number she has not said, it is a thing she means.** **The seventh first is the last first of a month she is ever going to get for nothing and she spent it on purpose.**
7. **THE FOURTEEN.** She came back to the rows and said out loud that the third of her three reasons had changed, because in twenty-five days the arithmetic is going to be public property on a stick at a frame two days of road west. **She is not going to tell the fourteen, and it is not any of the three reasons: it is that she wants it to be a fact in a county and not a thing a woman said, and that is a reason she would not put in front of anybody.** She went back to doing sums at the frame. The frame now has fourteen people at it and thirteen of them are not waiting for her, and about a third of the man at it is checked by a woman of thirty-four.
8. **NING WU, his second Volume 12 appearance, at ch 713 only, and the year is not mentioned once.** He is nineteen, he is in the third row about forty feet in, he has the hands of their father, he has carried stones for four men for nine years, and **he has never said her name to her since a road five miles west of a mill nine years ago and he did not say it.** She told him she has worked out her own total and he said *five years*: **he has worked out how many stones he has moved on that ground, four men, nine years, to the stone, and has never said the number and has nowhere in that ground it could go.** **They said the same sentence to each other from opposite ends of a row of stones: *there is not one person to give it to*.** He told her that a thing said at a frame is said by a person and a person can be asked, and a thing on a board is a thing in a county and a county does not get asked. **Nothing was settled. He did not call her anything and she did not call him anything.** `Ning Wu` is named once in the volume and this is it.
9. **THE MOUNTAIN, the last time in Volume 12.** Four hundred volumes on the shelves, nine sheets a day, **a locked drawer thirty feet away with the key in the front of her bag that she did not open**, a boy of sixteen who said *it is all right, I have never opened it, I do not know what is in it and I am not going to*, four bundles up that stair in thirty-one years, **and about a day and a half of oil in a stone jar under a bench for a lamp in a room she cannot get into.** She went up eight flights, put her eye to the grille, and **did not lift the bar.** She is not going to.
10. **AN OLD MAN WITH A SHUT BOOK went up the mountain road past the yard at the sixth hour of the sixteenth of the month beginning 2,264 and did not stop and did not look at her and did not answer her.** Alive, old, carrying a book, and **he was not going to the tower, because the road goes on past it. It was not to her and it was not about her and there was not one thing about it that she was owed.** He is never named in the volume. He holds no court, keeps no staff, threatens nobody and is not defeated. `thank` is 0 in this chapter and nobody was thanked in it.
11. **THE COUNT SHE WROTE HERSELF.** **A count takes a board and not a person**, and she has never in her life been counted where she stands, and everything that has ever come off her has come off her in a place she was not in, from a hand that was not hers, on a day she did not choose. **The only thing that can be counted at a first of a month is a line.** And the count she cannot escape is the one she wrote herself: the name on a slate on the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2,054, four sentences on a board on the eighteenth of the month beginning 2,114, and a line in thirteen days.
12. **SOMETHING SETTLED, once in this batch, and she noticed it on the mountain road on the eighteenth of the month beginning 2,264.** It comes out of **the ground under her feet and not out of her hands** — not off two coppers, not off a bag, not off an arm, not off the place behind her fourth rib, not off four counts of breath. It arrives on no day she can point to, she has no instrument for it and is not going to ask for one, **and it is the first thing in nineteen years she has decided not to count.** **No figure of what is left of him is stated anywhere in this batch or in the volume, and the settling is on listed work cleared past the line and never on a death.**
13. **IMMORTAL VESSEL 3, at ch 716, day 2,290, the twenty-seventh of the month beginning 2,264, at the second hour, standing at the end of a counter in a room with the shutters up and a hundred people reading behind her.** **2,290 − 2,206 = 84, and the six on top of seventy-eight is because there is a date on this one and the date has to be a first.** Taken in nine seconds. No announcement, no voice, no line anywhere, and a hundred people did not look up.
14. **THE THIRD VOLUME 12 COST, named once, at ch 716, and not re-explained in ch 717–720: SHE CANNOT BE COUNTED WHERE SHE STANDS.** Said in the ordinary voice in the mouth of the man of sixty-five with the book and **never in hers, and she says on the page that she has not said that sentence in her own mouth and is not going to.** The count is a count of boards and has never been a count of people in eleven hundred years; **she is not on the board; there is not one thing in this county that can put her in one; the harvest takes a board and it has never taken a person and there is no instrument in the world that knows how.**
15. **THE ROAD A LINE TRAVELS, from the man of sixty-five with the book.** A slate at a turn goes up a road to the seat once a month on a cart with about forty other boards in it, and four people at the seat have never looked at one of them. A bundle goes up a stair in a tower four miles up a mountain from the square once a month on the arm of a man who has carried four in thirty-one years. **Not one person in that building is on that road and not one person in that building has ever been asked to look.**
16. **THE EIGHTH FIRST, day 2,294, at the first hour, at the two posts, outdoors, in daylight.** Three people inside a hundred yards and a fourth four hundred yards west, and she counted all four before she took anything out of the bag. **She wrote with the right hand on an arm that was open, with a nib and a cake of ink that has not been let dry since the seventh of the month beginning 1,874, and she did not lift the nib** — a nib laid on cold slate and not lifted takes, and one that is lifted and put back does not, and that is why one is never written twice. **The line is nineteen words: *Ning Yan, the two posts. Two hundred and eighteen days. One in twenty. Ten days, twenty-one hours, thirty-six minutes.* And the same sum under it in figures and again in words, so a person who cannot do the arithmetic can check it without doing the arithmetic.**
17. **THE HAND.** **The little finger of her right hand stopped being part of her hand somewhere in the middle of that line.** No mark, no blood, she can move it and it does not go where she puts it. **Three fingers and a thumb at the last page of Volume 12. The arm did not close afterwards and there is no closing it, and it was still open at the third hour of the seventh of the month beginning 2,294 five days later.** She picked the bar up out of the grit in a count of twenty-nine, which is the same twenty-nine it has always been, which is the part she found unbearable.
18. **THE NINE SECONDS.** At that frame, after the cart had gone west with the board on it, there was a sound in the air for about nine seconds, not loud, not inside her head and not outside it, and it was there for all four people. **It is never printed in the book — not in brackets, not in quotation marks, not in italics — and it is rendered entirely as what it does to the people who hear it.** Four people give four accounts and no two of them agree: **a man of forty-nine who will not say what he heard and says he has not got it right yet and has four columns to write · a woman of sixty who says it was a number · a carter of about fifty who says it was nothing, that he was three hundred yards off and heard his own axle, and that his boy heard it · a boy of nine who says it was him.** **She is not one of the four and she has told nobody what she heard, because the day she tells it is the day there is one account.**
19. **THE HARVEST AND THE BILL, ch 718, the batch's irreversible step.** The levy is one in twenty of every day a name has had in a column, it has been coming off her since the ninth hour of the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2,054 at a day and a half a month, and **it is not something that happens to a board. She wrote a figure that the levy had already taken, so it has come off the writing and it has not come off her again.** **The harvest took a board and did not take a person, and there is no instrument in this county that knows how to take a person off a piece of wood. And there is no instrument in the world that takes a line out of a book that has already gone up a stair.** And: **the bill for Court is settled.** The thing that reads records did not read the board at the north end of the rows; **it wanted a shape with a hand on it, and it has one, and it went up a stair at the second hour of the first of the month beginning 2,294 in a bundle with about forty other boards, and a room at the top of a stair four miles up a mountain has read it. She did not agree to it, she has said she would have written it anyway, and she said out loud at a frame in daylight that she is not going to be able to write a line that does not have her name at the end of it ever again.**
20. **THE STAIR AND THE THRESHOLD.** Eight flights and forty steps with a bar nine feet nine, the shoulder going at about the three hundredth step of the first four, and nine counts of breath at the third landing of the second four and a window about two feet across that has not been opened. The low door is standing open. **The bar is on the floor inside the room, flat, against the wall on the left, and the dust on the top of it is broken at one end and not at the other, and nothing in Volume 12 explains it.** There is a long table down the middle, a lamp in a cage burning at the far end, and a second stair going up out of the far side. **She went up one step at the third hour of the seventh of the month beginning 2,294, and stood on it for a count of forty, and did not go up the second one.** **There is nothing in that room she can put a figure to, and that is the first time in nineteen years anything has been in front of her that she could not measure, and she went up the step anyway.**

### How far the rows sit past the wall: the open finding, carried again and NOT settled

**STILL OPEN AND NOT SETTLED BY THIS BATCH.** `state/current.md` has carried *how far the rows sit past the wall* as open since the Volume 11 close and `outline/volume-12.md` §*Major locations* says the same thing in the same words. **Batch 0004 puts no mile figure on the rows leg in either direction, and the batch's own measurement of it is two days of road, which is ch 712's timing and not a claim about distance.**

**THE UNIT RULE, RESTATED AND STILL BINDING: THIRTEEN MILES IS THE WALL TO THE TURN AND MAY BE SAID IN MILES. TWO DAYS OF ROAD IS THE ROWS TO THE TURN AND MAY NOT BE GIVEN A MILE FIGURE IN EITHER DIRECTION. TWO MILES OF FLAT IS THE GROUND TO THE WALL PAST THE GATE AND MAY BE. FOUR MILES IS THE SQUARE TO THE TOP OF THE MOUNTAIN AND MAY BE.**

**Two new facts this batch put on the page, both about the tower and neither about the turn.** The store road goes west out of the turn for **nine miles to a post**, and after that it stops being a road anybody pays for, and then it is **four miles up**; and the mountain road is wide enough for two people going in opposite directions, which is where the old man passed her.

### The running ledger — at the last page of Volume 12, day 2,300

- **Ning Yan — IMMORTAL VESSEL 3**, taken at ch 716, day 2,290. **Nineteen.** A bar nine feet nine **with no strap on it**, costing twenty-two to fifty-four counts every time. **Three fingers and a thumb, the index gone since Volume 1 and the little finger gone at ch 717.** Right arm open four days in five and open on the eighth first as well. Four counts of breath with seven on a rise and nine standing still at the top of eight flights. The small open place low behind her fourth rib, the size of a coin. **Seven hundred and forty days lighter and not one day of it gone back. Not hungry.**
- **Against her ribs: one object.** A book of eight leaves made out of a blanket, a date and a place on the first, four sentences on the second, `YUAN SHENG` on the third in four capital strokes in her own hand, and five blank that are hers. **She has never called it anything and Volume 12 closes with it still not named.**
- **In a bag at the bottom of a stair:** a dish, a lump of clay, a ring the width of a finger, a stub of a nib, a cake of ink opened on the seventh of the month beginning 1,874 and never let dry, a key to a locked drawer she has not used since the eleventh of the month beginning 2,054, and a strip of hand-made paper nine inches long with eighty-one lines on it and the same sum written underneath in words.
- **In a book above her:** nineteen words in her own hand with a date and a place on them, true, and a copy of the same figure in a pencil column in a county hand on the other side of a slate that faces a wall.
- **Against the inside of a county hand and her own:** a record kept out loud with six terms and no seventh, the fifth term unenforceable and known to be so, **and a bill that was raised at ch 688, never answered at the time, and settled at ch 718 by a shape going up a stair in a hand and not by a mouth.**
- **Yuan.** **Court, from ch 687.** Present tense, no figure of what is left of him anywhere in the volume, one frame scene at ch 694 and none since. **Something settled once, on listed work cleared past the line, out of the ground under her feet and not out of her hands, and she decided not to count it.**
- **Four miles up a mountain:** a room with a long table in it, a lamp in a cage burning at the far end of it, a bar on the floor inside with the dust broken at one end, and a second stair going up out of the far side, seven steps visible and then not. **She is on the first of them.**
- **Two days of road east, in a ground of two hundred people:** a board with four men writing a stroke and a number each, four a night, **six hundred and eighty-eight of them at day 2,300, which is `(2,300 − 2,128) × 4`,** and a line in her own hand that not one of the four can read. **She last counted it at day 2,274 and it was five hundred and eighty-four.** **Thirteen people at a frame who do not need her.** A brother forty feet in who has counted four thousand stones a day for five years and gave the number to one person and will not give it again.
- **Thirteen miles west, at a turn:** two posts, a rail, a slate with her name in a county hand and thirty days beside it and a figure on the other side that faces a wall, a woman of sixty on a bench four hundred yards west whose name is the fourth from the bottom of the fourth column of that slate, and a man of forty-nine with a rag and a stick of white chalk who has been writing a levy for nineteen years and does not know he is writing one.
- **The volume's question, answered at ch 718:** *whether a designation made to be harvested can be carried up instead.* **It can. It has to be carried by a piece of paper and not by a person, because a person cannot be counted where she stands and cannot keep what she finds by holding it, and because the only instrument in the world that takes a person through a wall is a thing seen truly and written truly.**
- **What Volume 13 opens on:** **she is at the top of a stair; the announcement has gone into the ground nine times and went up this time carrying a shape; four people within four hundred yards of that frame heard nine seconds of it and no two of them agree; a figure of her own is in a book that does not need her alive to be right; and whatever is up there knows exactly what she is and what it cost her to be it, and does not know her.**

sentences carrying it across five chapters of Batches 0001–0002 and withdrew it the same way, asserting nothing in its place:** `grep -oin 'twenty miles' chapters/volume-12/*.md` now returns **0** — ch 676 ×3, ch 677 ×2, ch 685, ch 686 and ch 689 all read **two days of road** where they read twenty miles, and `grep -oi 'two days of road' chapters/volume-12/*.md` returns **38**. **How far the rows stands. **What ch 676's numbers are built on, and what the close's review pass had to repair because the withdrawal above made them checkable: the turn to the wall is thirteen miles and the made road runs on three miles past it to the ground at sixteen, so the made road is fourteen miles and the two miles of flat are the only two miles on the whole leg that no one made — which is what ch 677's fourteen is and why it is not the odd figure out.** The strap parts six miles east of the turn on the fourth of the six days and the wall is thirteen miles east of the turn, so the three days she carries the bar in one hand run from six to thirteen: **seven miles, and ch 676's *eleven* was wrong and is now seven.** ch 676's hours were wrong in the same paragraph and are now one clock: **she is at the gate on the morning of the seventh and says the figure out loud there at the fourth hour, crosses the flat from that hour, arrives at the wall at the second hour of the next day, goes through it at the second hour of the eighth, is in the rows at the fourth hour of the eighth and puts the bar down on the flat at the ninth hour** — which is what lines 3, 41, 43, 51, 59, 77 and 105 now say between them, and which they did not say before the review (the opening line had her two miles short of the wall and through it in the same hour, and the eighth hour of the seventh came after the hour she had already crossed the flat at).

### The volume's findings, audited against the page

1. Being visible and being safe are the same question in this world, and it costs the hand she wrote the answer with — three fingers and a thumb at the last page.
2. A count takes a board and not a person, and has never in eleven hundred years taken a person, and there is no instrument in the world that knows how.
3. A designation made to be harvested can be carried up instead — on paper, in a hand, with a date and a place, saying a true thing, written once because nobody writes one twice.
4. A line, once true and down and readable, belongs to whoever keeps it, and does not come back (ch 708, asked and answered).
5. She cannot stop counting, and this is the first thing in nineteen years she has decided not to count (ch 715) — a settlement out of the ground under her feet and not out of her hands.
6. An announcement is not made to be heard. It is made to arrive, and it arrives where there is something to receive it (ch 702–703, ch 718).
7. A figure is not a person, and nothing on a board a person can be collected off is a person (ch 709, ch 717).

### Ending, as the plan has it

§*Volume climax*, §*Concrete resolution* and §*Final chapter image* are delivered on the page: the eighth first, day 2,294, first hour, two posts, outdoors, daylight, open right arm — nineteen words in her own hand with a date and a place, true, nobody writing one twice, the little finger stopping mid-line, the arm never closing, seven hundred and forty days lighter with none going back. The board up at the second hour with the fraction off before it went up; the harvest a board and not a person; nine seconds of sound and four accounts inside four hundred yards over a day and a half with no two agreeing, the announcement printed nowhere, and she is not one of the four. The bill for Court settled on listed work by a shape with a hand on it read in a room four miles up a mountain — unagreed and would-have-written-anyway, and no line without her name at the end of it ever again. And she went up: eight flights and eight hundred and eighty steps with a bar nine feet nine, fifty-four counts to set it down, nine counts of breath on the third landing of the second four, the low door open on the seventh of the month beginning 2,294, the bar on the floor inside with the dust broken at one end and not at the other, the long table, the lamp in a cage, the second stair out of the far side. **She went up one step. That is the last thing in Volume 12.**
