### The eight structural decisions, in one line each, so a review can walk them

| # | Decision | Line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1** | What the Court is | **The receiving end of the announcement layer, in a room, with a lamp in a cage and no chairs — Feng Lushi's job with the ceiling taken off**, and ch 719 put the no-chairs on the page one chapter before Volume 12 turned |
| **D2** | What *decides* means | **Above the line a thing is whatever the last hand at the table wrote in the row for it; there is one instrument and it is a hand; the deciding takes one look and there is no second and no appeal. A thing that arrives with no row is not refused, it is administered** |
| **D3** | Being small, shown three ways | **She cannot reach the table and every chapter in the room shows her get a hand on the edge of it or not · nobody above the line counts days because nobody above the line loses them and she is still losing them at one hour and twelve minutes a day and cannot see the day turn · every price she has paid is invisible to everybody making the decision** |
| **D4** | The lamp | **Not an oil lamp; no oil in the building for nine years. Fed by hand; every entry costs a feed; there is a mark on the lamp and the rule is the mark, the practice is the first of a month, and the two have agreed for four hundred years only because the lamp wants twenty-nine days to the mark and a month is thirty. She gets the twenty-nine off the lamp's own rate of descent and not by counting days between two feeds, because the only two she sees are exactly thirty apart. The room counts in hands and she counts in days and the two have never agreed. She learns what feeding it costs and who is charged by it, in the single instance of herself, and does not learn what it is paying for** |
| **D5** | The row, and the figure at the head of it | **The figure at the head of her row is her own total — ten days, twenty-one hours and thirty-six minutes, in the hand she wrote it in at ch 717 and carried up the stair at ch 718. There is no stage on it and no name on it, and it is still growing at one hour and twelve minutes a day, and above the line nobody loses a day, so nobody there could ever know the row is going stale. She writes her own stage under it in Batch 0003 and a row with a person on it is a row that gets counted** |
| **D6** | The three stage costs | **Immortal Vessel 4 — she cannot be given a thing · 5 — she cannot be measured with a person · 6 — she cannot be looked at again. Named once each, in their own chapter, never re-explained** |
| **D7** | How a stage is taken with no board, no slate and no counter | **A stage is written in a row by a hand in the light of a lamp that has to be fed to be lit, on a day the feeder chooses — so every interval has to be counted twice, in days by her and in feeds by the room, and the two have never agreed** |
| **D8** | The second place at the table | **Two places at the long table; one occupied for four hundred years; the other not a chair, not a seat, addressed, and the right size for him. Nobody put him in it. It is Volume 14 and this volume does not open it** |

### What the page now holds that Volume 12 did not

1. **There is a person in that room** and they did not appear in any of the nine times she counted the room through the grille, because the lamp is on a shelf at the far end and the light goes away from the door. They have both hands on the near edge of the table and have not moved once, and have never once looked up, and have never once spoken, and **they did not speak in this batch at all.**
2. **The second stair goes up and comes back down to the floor of the same room**, out of a place in the wall behind the lamp's shelf. That is why seven steps are visible from the door. She counts it to **nine hundred** and loses the count there. **The whole is nine hundred and four and she does not have that figure until ch 754**, and nothing in this batch adds it to the tower's own eight hundred and eighty.
3. **The table is four feet high and she can get a hand on the edge and can get up on it** (four tries, days 2,313–2,316), and can walk its top on her hands and knees. She chose not to put a hand on it while forty boards were on it in front of the person who reads them.
4. **The lamp is not an oil lamp**: no dish, no bowl, no reservoir, no wick, no key, no door in the side, nothing on the shelf, wall behind the light, and **the flame does not lean when her hand passes it sixty times in a room with a door standing open.**
5. **The mark is a short line cut into the stone of the wall behind and a hand's breadth to the left of the lamp**, the same cut as the table and the shelf, and the light stops on it and does not go under it.
6. **The instrument of the room is a stroke and a figure and one look, at four to a minute.** Forty boards is ten minutes; the bundle of papers is three times that; the whole of a month is forty minutes. **The room does not read boards**: one stroke in the same corner and one figure of the same shape on all forty, which she read with her fingers in the dark under the table over four days.
7. **The row.** Off the table, under it, flat on stone, face up, a foot long and two inches across. A head, a column, one figure in the column. **Ten days, twenty-one hours and thirty-six minutes, in her own hand**, because a figure copied any other way than it was written is not that figure and this room has been putting figures in a column for four hundred years. **No name, no place, no date and nothing about what she is on it.**
8. **The rate.** Two of her own hand (three fingers and a thumb, laid flat, edge on) a day. Fifty-eight of her own hand from the top of the cage to the cut in the wall. **Fifty-eight divided by two is twenty-nine**, done four times, standing, out loud. Twenty-nine days from the first of a month is the thirtieth, and the next turning is on the first of the next, and **so there is one day in every month in which that lamp stands on the line with nothing above it and nothing below it, and there has not been one of those days used for four hundred years.** The mark from the feed on 2,324 is **2,353, eight days from 2,345.** The mark from the feed on 2,354 is **2,383, twenty-seven days from 2,356 and twenty-six days from 2,357**, and the next bundle is 2,384.
9. **The turnings are not on a schedule.** The turning on **2,351, the twenty-eighth of the month beginning 2,324, came two days before her own sum said the line would be reached.** Intervals seen: 2,324 → 2,351 is twenty-seven days, and 2,351 → 2,354 is three days. The room counts in hands and she counts in days and **the two have never agreed, because a hand turns a lamp as often as it has to and no hand has ever written down how often that is.** The card 733's *the lamp is turned down to a mark and turned back up* is rendered as a hand going up between four bars and closing on the base of the light.
10. **A turning takes eleven seconds and the arm that turns it is smaller afterwards by the width of the little finger on her left hand**, and the distance the light comes up that wall is the same distance the arm goes down. **The same substance.** She does not learn what it is and she does not learn what the lamp is paying for, and no mouth in this batch told her and none may in this volume.
11. **The second place at the table** is found at ch 724: a stretch of the far side the length of her own forearm, paler and smoother, with a shape worn into it that is not a mark anybody made with a tool, and nothing in front of it and nothing on it. **She does not touch it, does not name it, and says not one word about it out loud.** It is the first thing in Volume 13 she has left alone on purpose and it is Batch 0003's frame scene at ch 758 and Batch 0004's.
12. **The bar is left flat against the wall on the left of the room at ch 731, broken end towards the door**, by her own hand, on purpose, and it is there at the last page of this batch and is the bar Batch 0003 goes down without. **The bar is still dated nowhere and she took it up when she was nine, and the only two statements about its origin in the manuscript remain ch 670 and ch 720.**
13. **She has spent a day.** The fifth blank leaves against her ribs are still blank, nothing from this room has gone into them, she said so out loud at ch 721 standing in daylight and did not improve on it, and she said it again at ch 735.

### What the page now holds that Batch 0001 did not

1. **The boy of sixteen is on the page**, and he is the batch's pressure made visible. He came up eight hundred and eighty steps in the dark at the sixth hour of **2,361**, out of breath, having not been up that stair in nine years, **because the lamp on the fourth landing went out on the third of the month beginning 2,294 and there is no oil in the building**, and he asked one question: why the lamp at the top of this tower is still lit when the lamp he was told to keep going is not. **She could not answer it**, and she said so out loud in that room, and that is the first time in nineteen years a person has come to her with a question and she has had nothing for it. Nobody above the line sent him. He went down again on **2,387** with her counting all eight hundred and eighty out loud and a number instead of an answer, and he came back up a third time on **2,413** because he has been asked twice, has said he does not know twice, and the man who counts the boards at the far end of that floor has started asking instead. **He is not clever and he is not a voice for anything.** He gets up on that four-foot table in one movement and she cannot, he cannot get under it and she can, he cannot read a strip of wood by touch and she can, and he counted forty boards coming off a table in ten minutes on his own at 2,384 and she had been the only person in every room who could do that for nineteen years.
2. **She cannot reach the table and he can** (ch 737), shown once, in a room where one look decides everything. **Nothing in that room sees anybody standing on it** — she has been on it twice and he stood on the middle of it for a count of nine and the person at the table did not look up, and that is the truest thing she has about the place and she did not know it until he did it.
3. **There are four rows under that table** (ch 738). Four strips of pale wood, a foot long and two inches across, face up on the stone, every one with a head at one end that is a figure and every one with a column. **The column is a column of figures and not a list of things**, established from the width of the cuts and the absence of any stroke with a turn in it on the three old ones. **Three of them have gone soft at every edge and one of them is hers and is two months old**, and she can say they are older by a great deal and cannot say how much and is not going to guess.
4. **THE ROW RULE, found from the furniture at the midpoint, ch 743, day 2,392.** **A hand at a table cannot enter anybody into anything.** There is nothing on that table to write with — no ink, no stone, no sand, no pen, no holder, no knife, no rag, no blotter — so a hand that decides what a thing is has nothing to write it down with, and this hand copies exactly. Her figure came out of her row in her own hand with three fingers and a thumb on the nib, and she chose it at two posts on a road at the first hour of 2,294 before it was on a board. **So the head of a row is chosen by the person the row is about, in another room, standing up, out loud, and the hand writes what the person says and nothing else.** And **who keeps it: the room stands on it.** The table is four feet above it and nothing goes between them.
5. **Nobody above the line remembers making that rule and nobody ever will.** She found it by the age of the strips and by the absence of anything in the room that says why. She says out loud that a rule kept exactly for four hundred years has nobody left in the building who was in the room on the day it started, and that the reason the rule exists is the reason she needs it — a hand cannot enter a person, so nobody in that building can decide what a person is — and that she is not going to be able to ask, because the only way to ask a question in that building is to put it in a row and she had not got one.
6. **She said a row out loud at 2,393 and a hand wrote on a board** (ch 744), standing, in daylight, in the ordinary voice, one figure: **eight hundred and thirty-four**. It is not taken and it is not refused, the hand does not know it was hers, and she is not going to read what it wrote and says why out loud. **The board went up that stair on the first of the month beginning 2,414 with the next bundle and came back down empty like every other board, and she is not going to find out what is in it for a very long time.**
7. **What a row costs, ch 745.** She took six readings of that forearm. **Forty boards in ten minutes and a bundle in thirty cost that arm nothing.** **One figure copied exactly cost the same as one lamp** — the width of the little finger on her left hand — and she was watching the writing and did not take a sixth reading until the next day, and she says out loud that that is the only thing in ninety-nine days she has got wrong that she could have got right. **The saying is free and the writing is not, and the cost comes off the hand that writes.** And the reversal: **there is no limit on it.** She can say a row as many times as she has days for and nobody will stop her and nobody will be angry.
8. **IMMORTAL VESSEL 4, day 2,403, the twentieth of the month beginning 2,384, at one hundred and thirteen days, and its cost named once: she cannot be given a thing.** There is no board above the line, no slate, no counter and no ground; a stage is taken by being written in a row by a hand in the light of that lamp on a day the feeder chooses. **She is not entered, so there is nothing to hand it to, so she got a board out of the stack under the table herself, went up on the table at the near end, went twenty-two paces along it on her hands and knees, knelt on the shelf and wrote a figure in her own hand with three fingers and a thumb on an arm that has been open since the first of the month beginning 2,294.** No announcement, no sound, no tribulation, and the person at the table did not look up. **Seven of eleven holds where it was eight, and she could not work out where the day went off her and did not guess in a room where a hand copies figures exactly.** **She says the interval out loud: 2,206 − 2,128 = 78 and 2,290 − 2,206 = 84 and 2,403 − 2,290 = 113, and it is a hundred and thirteen and not seventy-eight because a stage past the third working point is taken against a row and there was no row to take it against.**
9. **The one at the table goes out of the room four times in four days** (ch 748), and she was under the table every one of them. The outline's §D6 pins this to Batch 0002. **She does not follow and does not stand in the doorway**, and she names the carried cost she has not said out loud in nineteen years: a room that is expecting somebody cannot be met by her.
10. **`Yuan Sheng` said out loud at the tenth hour of 2,411** (ch 748), standing, in daylight, in the ordinary voice, on the floor at the near end of the long table, in a room with a person in it. **In the ten seconds before she said it he asked her not to — one question, in the ordinary voice, standing, in daylight: *Is there a way to do this that does not have me in it.* She did not answer it and she said it anyway.** The hands came off the near edge for the first time in a hundred and twenty days with nothing on the table, a board came out of the stack and was not the top one, and a stroke went onto it and something else went onto it. **He did not ask a second time and he did not hide it.** He said what it is and what it costs, in the ordinary voice, standing, in daylight, and he said that a name is easier to find than a shape and that the thing that reads records does not speak when it finds something. **She then said the six terms out loud in that room, one at a time, standing, in daylight, as she has said them in every room she has ever said them in, and there was not a seventh one and she did not ask for one.**
11. **He is found at 2,414 and nothing speaks to him** (ch 749). The board went up the stair on the first with forty others. She worked it out in her own voice and waited two full days for something and nothing came, and there was no mark on that table and no stroke and no figure anywhere and no hand came off the near edge except for the boards. **She does not tell the boy and says why in one line.** He notices the second place at the table — the pale stretch on the far side, the shape worn into it, the absence of any chair — and she **does not say one word about it out loud** and tells him not to touch the table.
12. **She works out what she would have to do about the light at 2,420 and does not do it** (ch 750). One day into the cage buys one day. She could hold that lamp off the line for a year out of eight hundred and sixty-one. **She is not going to, because she has no instrument for what came out and because she has a row in that room and does not know what it is for.** The chapter ends on the one thing she has not been able to work out in a hundred and nineteen days: **what a row that has her in it is for.**

### The four arithmetic and dating faults on the page

Ch 746 and ch 747 showed neither.** He cannot be put in the room: he went down on 2,387 and came back up on 2,413, and ch 746 runs 2,403–2,404 and ch 747 runs 2,405–2,408. **The second half of the clause was used instead, and one line was added to each chapter, both in the room and out loud.**

- **ch 747**, in the twenty-fifth's section, where she will not say the two words until she knows a day: *the boy of sixteen came up eight hundred and eighty steps to ask me one question and I gave him a number, and a hand that copies figures exactly is not going to take his word for one word of it, and there is not one thing I could do with him afterwards that would make it true that I said it, and I am not going to spend one of those four days finding out whether he would.* He is the only person on either side of the line who could testify to the saying of it, and a room where one look decides everything will not take his word. **He stays below the line, nothing is offered to him, and no beat of the batch moved.**

### What the page now holds that Batch 0002 did not

1. **The instrument in that room is a person, and every figure in that room is a comparison and not a measurement.** A row has two ends, the head is a figure and the column is figures, and every figure at the head was said out loud by a person in some other room and came up a stair in an armful, so it has been moved and not weighed. There is no number in that building for a figure to be more than or less than. **The only thing it can be measured against is the one body at the table, and that body has been the same one for four hundred years, so every figure that has ever gone into a column in that room is a statement about that arm.** She says out loud that there is a person at the far end of that table who has spent themselves keeping that county's arithmetic in order and has not been told, once, in four hundred years, that every number they have written down is a number about them.
2. **She cannot be measured where she stands, and she works out why: being looked at is what holds a person still, and there is not one thing in that building looking at her.** She can manage a count of eleven holding still the way the one at the table holds still.
3. **THE SECOND STAIR IS NINE HUNDRED AND FOUR, AND SHE HAS IT.** She goes down it on the twenty-third of the month beginning 2,414 with nothing in either hand and comes back up the whole way, and the number is the same going up as it came down. **The four steps she could not hold at ch 723 are the first four out of the floor of the room, not the last four**, and **there is no nine hundred and fifth, because the stair goes up out of the room and comes back down into the floor of the same room and has two ends in here.** She says out loud that she was using the number as a reason for five months and that not being able to hold a figure is not the same as there being something in the way. **The two stairs are not added anywhere and 904 and 880 are never put in the same sum.**
4. **She has a stub of a nib and a cake of ink.** Picked up off the copying floor on the twelfth of the month beginning 2,414 and carried up eight hundred and eighty steps inside her shirt against the fourth rib. **The ch 734 decision is carried and acted on, not re-decided and not reversed**: she names all nine things in the bag out loud, takes two of them, says out loud that the decision was never about the nib or the ink but about the drawer, and **says out loud on the fifteenth that she is not going down the second stair for anything until she can do it in one push and is not going to try it in one push until she knows how long it is.** The key, the dish, the clay, the ring and the nine inches of hand-made paper are still in the bag and the locked drawer is still unopened.
5. **The mark falls on a first of a month and not on a thirtieth, for the second time in four hundred years, and it is her own doing.** Twenty-nine days from a turning is a thirtieth when the turning is on a first and a first when the turning is on a second, and the last turning was on the second of the month beginning 2,414 because of the day she spent into that cage on the fourth of the month beginning 2,354. **And the reversal she did not intend: she bought one day with a day and what she bought was the loss of the one day of slack every month has had for four hundred years.**
6. **The room's instrument ran off her arm for the first time in four hundred years.** She puts herself where the arms go and says a row out loud about what she is, and at the ninth hour of the twelfth of the month beginning 2,444 the hands come off the near edge with nothing in front of them, come down the leg of the table, close on her open right forearm at the wrist, go its length once and hold on the wrist bone for about eleven seconds. **Her forearm goes down by the width of the little finger on her left hand — the same width the one at the table pays every time that lamp is turned — and this is the first time in four hundred years the cost has come off anything except the person standing at the table.** A stroke and a figure go onto a board, **the figure is ten days, twenty-one hours and thirty-six minutes, and she said her age and the room wrote down what she cost.**
7. **IMMORTAL VESSEL 5 at ch 761, day 2,461, the eighteenth of the month beginning 2,444, at fifty-eight days, and its cost named once: she cannot be measured with a person.** She writes **five** with the nib, in her own hand, on an open arm, three fingers and a thumb, on the shelf in front of that lamp. The interval is said out loud and the reason for it is said out loud: **the first three were taken against a room and a room is not a row, and the fourth was a hundred and thirteen because there was no row to take it against.** A comparison takes two things standing still and **so from today the thing that does the measuring will be her and the thing being measured will be a record, and if there is a person in it, that person is furniture.** Seven of eleven holds, unchanged all day, and she does not guess why. No announcement, no sound, no tribulation, and nobody looked up.
8. **THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE STEP, ch 763.** Her own strip of pale wood comes off the stone under that table for the first time in one hundred and seventy-one days, **she refuses a board out of the stack and says why in one sentence**, and she writes **five** in the second pair of cuts down in the column, under the price, with the nib, in her own hand, standing, in daylight, in the ordinary voice. **Her own forearm goes down by the width of the little finger on her left hand while the nib is still on the wood, because the cost of the writing comes off the hand that writes, and the hand that wrote it was hers.** A figure that is a price can only be added up and a figure that is a person can only be counted, **being counted is the thing she has been escaping since she was nine years old**, and she says out loud that being entered is not the same as being rescued and that she did not put it there so that something would come and take it out.
9. **The column cannot be used and cannot be undone.** Fourteen pairs of cuts, one with the price and one with five and twelve empty, and **not one second figure in any of the other three strips in that room in four hundred years and not one empty pair of cuts in any of them.** Ten days, twenty-one hours and thirty-six minutes and five is not a figure. **And the two figures go out of date in different currencies: the price at one hour and twelve minutes a day, and five from the day after the sixth stage, which is a day a hand in the light of that lamp chooses.** There is not one instrument in the world that puts either of them right.
10. **THE NINTH FRAME SCENE, ch 758, and it is the first in the manuscript that is about a place he could get into.** He is in the room, he has no weight, and **he is smaller than the table is tall and no figure of that is given.** There are two places at that table and the far one has twenty-two paces of nothing on it and then a stretch the length of a forearm, paler and smoother, with a shape worn into it that no tool made, **and the shape is not a hand.** It is the right size for him, it is addressed, and nobody put him in it. **He does not get into it and he does not say no to it.** He says in the present tense that it is a piece of furniture and that he is not going to say yes to it either, because not one instruction in that room put him in it and there is not one person in that room he would be able to say no to. **Every sentence he speaks in it is in the present tense and no other character is in a marked present frame anywhere in Volume 13. There is no frame scene in any other chapter of ch 751–765 and no tenth anywhere in ch 721–780.**
11. **Ning Wu, once, at ch 765, and it is not a visit.** She says his name out loud for the first time in nine years above the line, at the ninth hour of the sixth of the month beginning 2,474. He is two days of road and six hundred feet below her. She says she is not going to, and that it is not a promise and it is a figure, and **that it is the first thing she has decided in nineteen years that no mouth in this building asked her about and nothing was going to undo for her.** He settles nothing, he is not on a page of any book, and the year is not named once.
12. **The boy of sixteen is in every chapter of the batch and is in the room for none of them.** He came up three times in Batch 0002 and went down on 2,417. What the batch shows is what he cannot do: he cannot be measured, he cannot be put in a column, what he is good at is worth nothing in that room, she cannot go down and put nine hundred and four on a strip of hand-made paper and hand it to him, he would not know what it was for either, and **she says out loud at ch 765 that she is not going down to tell him what a row is.** Nothing was offered to him in fifteen chapters and he is still below the line at the last page.

### What the page now holds that Batch 0003 did not

1. **THE FIRST LOOK, at ch 769, the seventeenth of that month, and it is the look at a foot of pale wood and not at her.** She gets a board out of the stack, puts her own strip on the top of the table at the near end, and says the whole of that row out loud on the shelf in front of the lamp because **the hand writes what a person said and nothing else.** The head comes down over the wood for about eleven seconds, a board comes out of the forty, and a stroke and a figure go onto it: **her price again, at the head and in the column, and not one stroke in the second pair of cuts.** She cannot tell whether the look saw the five. **And the ch 758 finding is paid: she stands still for eleven counts for the first time in a hundred and eighty-four days, and the reason is not that she has got better at it, it is that something had its attention on the shelf she was kneeling on.**
2. **A room that writes a figure twice has decided it twice, and two decisions are one decision.** She works that out at ch 770 and it is the finding that turns the batch: the price at the head of her row has now been decided twice in two hundred and two days and it has not moved a minute in either direction.
3. **THE OFFER, ch 772, day 2,504 and day 2,505, and it is true in every part.** **The one at the table speaks for the first time in the volume** and does not turn round and does not look up and does not stop working. It says that there is a column in this county adding one day in twenty since the ninth hour of the twenty-fourth of the month beginning 2,054 with a figure at the head of it that has never once been in a row above the line; **that it can amend one row and has never amended one; that it will put that figure into hers, in the pair of cuts under the one she wrote, over what she wrote there; that it costs one feed; that the feed for that lamp is paid by the hand at that table out of itself once every twenty-nine days and an amending is not that, and that the feed would therefore be hers; that it has to be written in the light, and that the light comes down to that cut at the fourth hour of the first of the month beginning 2,534, and if a hand is not in that cage before it gets there it does not come up again; and that it is not going to put a day in there on its own and have nothing for it, which has not happened here in four hundred years.** And then the one thing nobody in that room has ever said to her: **if a name goes in that column then the figure she wrote stops being hers and becomes the column's, and a column is not a person, and you can argue with a person.** **The whole speech took about eleven seconds.** It used the word *Court* once, for the building, and `grep -oiw court` over `chapters/volume-13/*.md` now returns exactly 1. **They are not cruel, interested, hesitant or kind, they are correct, and it is the only kind thing that room has ever done to her, and that is why it is dangerous.**
4. **She says out loud what a row is, at ch 768, and it has never been done in this building before.** It came out in four pieces in a count of ninety and then a fifth one she has never worked out. The four pieces are a place a thing is decided about · a head that is a figure and a figure is what the thing costs · a hand that fills it in and writes what a person said · and a thing that arrives with no row is administered and waits. **The fifth piece is the column, and she has been saying *row* and meaning the head.**
5. **She counts what she has, at ch 773, standing, in daylight, out loud, in a room with two people in it.** Four fingers and a thumb · two coppers she cannot count · five blank leaves against her fourth rib · a record kept out loud with six terms and no seventh · **nine hundred and fifty days by `D − 1,559`, one of them gone into a lamp.** **And she does not count the bar, because the putting down of it is the only thing about it that is hers and everything else about it belongs to a man who got it when she was nine.** The finding is that four of the five are dead weight and the fifth is the only thing in the world that can be spent, **and that is the only thing she has ever had that anybody could spend, and she did not put it there. She was nine.**
6. **What the figure is for, at ch 774: light.** A figure that goes down is the only thing in the world that can pay for light, and a room is a place where a figure goes down, and **she worked that out on a barrow ground when she was nine with a bar in her hands and did not know then that it was a working out.** She has been in rooms for nineteen years and none of them had one, and she could not be given a thing and could not be measured and could not be counted where she stood, **and she did not know any of that was because of the figure.**
7. **The second of the six terms is in daylight, and there is no daylight in that room, and she has been saying it out loud in lamplight for two hundred and twenty-six days and did not know until the twenty-third of the month beginning 2,504 that she was getting it wrong.** This is the pivot of the refusal and it is not a re-derivation: the six terms are Batch 0002's and the finding about the second of them is this batch's, and it is made in her mouth at the ninth hour of the twenty-third and acted on at the fourth hour of the first of the month beginning 2,534.
8. **IMMORTAL VESSEL 6 at ch 776, day 2,524, the twenty-first of the month beginning 2,504, at sixty-three days, and its cost named once: she cannot be looked at again.** She takes a third board out of the stack herself, goes up the table, kneels on the shelf and writes **six** with the nib against her fourth rib, and her right forearm goes down by the width of the little finger on her left hand while the nib is still on the wood. **The interval is said out loud as arithmetic and not as a lesson and she does not have a rule for it: fifty-eight and a hundred and thirteen and sixty-three, and she has counted every day of two hundred and twenty-two of them and counting a thing every day is not the same as knowing when it happens. What she has instead of a rule is that she can hold still on a stone floor with nothing in the room, and she could not do it on the twentieth of that month and could not do it when she took the last one.**
9. **THE SECOND LOOK, at ch 776, on the instrument, and it takes eleven seconds and there is nothing she can do with her face.** They had not looked up once in the whole of the volume before it. **And nothing was written.** No board came out of the stack, no stroke and no figure went onto anything, and she says out loud that a room does not report what it looked at, a room reports what it wrote, **and what it wrote is a price.** And then the cost: she has wanted to be looked at since the seventh of the month beginning 2,474, she has had two looks in five days, one of them at a foot of pale wood and one of them at her, **and it is the last one there is going to be.** A thing she wanted, with no use for it.
10. **THE REFUSAL, at ch 777, the twenty-seventh of the month beginning 2,504, and it is not out of pride and she says so out loud so that it is on the record in her own mouth.** **The figure the amending would put in that column is the room's and is one she has never seen; the figure she wants standing is hers, a five, in her own hand, wrong the moment after it is written.** And the reason that is not pride: **there has not been one figure in that building for two hundred and twenty-eight days that got into a row that she had not said out loud in that room first, the room has never amended a row, and there is no instrument in the world that amends a row twice, so she would never be able to check it once.** Her hand cannot write a false line, she has kept it off nine hundred and fifty-four lines of a record in nineteen years, and the fourth of the six terms was made for exactly this case.
11. **THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE STEP, ch 778, the first of the month beginning 2,534.** She puts no hand into the cage. **At the second hour the man comes up the turn with forty boards and a bundle of papers, and the hands at the near edge of that table do not come off the wood, and forty things have arrived and the room has not looked at one of them.** She says *Take them back down*, and he does not ask why, and he goes back down eight hundred and eighty steps with the bundle **and that is the first time in four hundred years a bundle has gone back down that stair the way it came.** At the fourth hour **the light came down to the cut and did not stop on the cut and went under it, and went out**, and there is nothing in the world that can put it back: no oil in the building for nine years, the person at that table is the lamp and the lamp is the person, five blank leaves, a bag at the bottom of a stair, **and there is not one thing in this building that goes into a lamp in a cage.** The cut was never what stopped it. **A hand has gone into that cage within a day of the light reaching that cut every single time in four hundred years, and the one thing that cut has ever been is the place they stand and watch from.**
12. **What she paid for the light, which is the second of the six terms.** On the twenty-ninth of the month beginning 2,504 she says all six out loud one last time in daylight and says the second one and stops, and then says it anyway, and on the thirtieth she says it will be the last time she says the second one in that room. **She is not taking the other five back.**
13. **Nine hundred and four steps in the dark with nothing in either hand, ch 779, the sixth and the seventh of the month beginning 2,534, down and back up, and the four steps she could not hold are the first four out of the room.** The wall is four inches off and she cannot get anything off it. She says the numbers out loud the whole way. **And she counts it coming up and it is nine hundred and four and it is not the same stair as the one in the tower and the two of them are never added.**
14. **MERIT SETTLES ONCE IN VOLUME 13, at ch 779, on the page, off the ground the room stands on and not out of anything in her hands, and no figure of it is stated.** The bundle of papers under the far end of that table is corded round twice and not knotted and has been there since before she came to the room; on the second of the month beginning 2,534 she finds it under the second leg from the near end, and on the morning of the third she goes and finds it again with her hand because she cannot see it, **and it is under the third leg.** She says one sentence about it, in the dark, on the flat of her back on the stone: **something in that building has been paid for and she did not feel it go.** And then she says that she has no instrument, cannot tell what it was or whose it was or what it was worth, **and that she has said out loud in that building before today that she is the only thing in it that can pay for anything, and that is not true, and she does not know when it stopped being true.** **No frame scene was staged to carry it and no figure of what is left of him is stated anywhere in ch 721–780.**
15. **A boy of sixteen stands in the doorway of a room with a lamp in a cage at the far end of it that has gone out, ch 780, day 2,540, the seventh of the month beginning 2,534, at the seventh hour, having been on that tower's own stair since the second hour of the morning.** He has an oil lamp of his own and it is the first light in that room in six days, and it puts a hand's width of itself along the near end of that table and goes no further, **and the twenty-two paces from there to the far end stay exactly as they had been.** He looks at her and nothing in that room decides anything when he does it, **and it is the first time since the ninth hour of the twenty-first of the month beginning 2,504 that anything has looked at her.** He asks why it was lit. **She gives him the whole arithmetic and it is true and it is all of it and it is not one sentence.** He says that is not why. He walks about the table and finds the second place and says *that is worn by something being put in the same place a great many times over a very long time and it is not a hand*, and she says out loud, for the first time in the volume, that it is not a chair and it is addressed and it is the right size for somebody who is not here. **He asks whether there is anybody in the room, and she tells him about the one at that table who has stood at it for four hundred years, and that she does not know whether anything in there can tell the difference between a room with a person in it and a room with a lamp burning in it.** And the last line of Volume 13: **she had a sentence for him and has not got it, and she does not have an answer that is small.**
16. **She said his name out loud once more, on the fifth of the month beginning 2,534, in the dark, in the middle of the six terms, because a record has to say what it is between.** Nothing in that room made a sound. **There is not one thing in that room she can tell has heard anything, and she is not going down two days of road to find out what was written.** That is Volume 14's engine and it is on the page.

- **The unit rule held.** Thirteen miles, two days of road, two miles of flat and four miles are the inherited figures and are not restated. **No card in this batch states a distance between anything above the line and anything below it in any unit in any direction, including steps and including a count of breath.** The only things this batch counts above the line are **the tower's own stair at eight hundred and eighty in two runs of four hundred and forty** and **the second stair at nine hundred and four**, and **the two are never added and never appear in the same sum; ch 779 says so out loud.** Nine hundred and four is counted at ch 779 and is not a comparison and not a distance to anything below the line.
- **The stale county total *thirteen days* is not on the page in this batch**, and `grep -oi 'thirteen days'` over ch 766–780 returns 0; the volume-wide hits are all substrings of *eight hundred and thirteen days* and *a hundred and thirteen days* and were there before this batch.
- **`twenty-two days` returns 0 over the whole volume.** Two hits were written in the first draft as the substring in *two hundred and twenty-two days* and both were reworded before the batch was closed. **No card in this batch equated it to any dated interval.**
- **The four accounts of nine seconds and no fifth: no account is on the page in this batch and the batch adds no fifth.** **The 2,920 and the 301 of 912 are unattributed and are not mentioned. What a third of a name is is open and is not answered.**
- **How far the rows sit past the wall is not stated.**
- **The one at that table spoke exactly once in the whole volume, at ch 772, and said nothing that is not true, and did not ask her a question and did not wait for an answer.** **It was not made cruel, interested, hesitant or kind.** It was not made to answer anything she said. The man who brings the bundles said nothing at all and was not asked anything, and **the bundle going back down the stair is not asked about either.**
- **The bundle of papers under the far end of that table** had a hand into it five times by the end of this batch and was not pulled — three before this batch, on the seventh of the month beginning 2,324, in the month beginning 2,354 and on the third of the month beginning 2,414, and two more in ch 779, on the second and the morning of the third of the month beginning 2,534 — **and at ch 779 it is found against a different leg of the table than the one it was put against.**
- **The bar is dated nowhere and she took it up when she was nine.** It is against the left-hand wall of that room, she did not pick it up once in fifteen chapters, **and she names it in her own count of what she has and refuses to count it, at ch 773, and it is in that room at the last page, at ch 780.**
- **The four sheets of rice paper and the five blank leaves are in the locked drawer and the drawer is not opened in this batch.** The five blank leaves stay blank. **She measures the drawer at ch 768 and puts her fingers on the grey in the wood where a hand goes and does not open it, and the reason she gave at ch 762 still holds and is not restated.**
- **The Order is not a conspiracy and not a chamber and is not on the page. Nothing in Volume 13 explains what the money above that building is for. No clearance, seal or countersignature is named or implied. No harem, nothing a romance, and she never says her mother's name.**
- **Nothing this batch tells her what the lamp is, and nothing tells her what the lamp is paying for.** What the cut is for *is* on the page, at ch 778, and it is that it is the place they stand and watch from.
- **Em dashes: 0.** Volume 12 ran nine in sixty and all four batches of Volume 13 have run none.
- **Paragraphs: 676 in fifteen chapters, 13 over about 90 words, none over about 120, longest 106** at ch 779, against Batch 0003's 669 with 17 over ninety and none over 120. **This row was 675 and 14 and is now 676 and 13, and the move is the repair: ch 776 carried one paragraph of 121 words, the longest in the volume and a breach of the 120 ceiling that this row denied, and the Batch 0004 review repair broke it at the only beat it had, between the general sentence and the three *Not once* instances, which turned one 121-word paragraph into a 36-word paragraph and a 75-word paragraph. Nothing else in the batch moved.**

### What the Volume 13 close inherits, in one place

**ch 721–780, sixty chapters, 118,939 words of body prose on method B, average 1,982, day 2,301 to day 2,540, three stages, eight firsts of a month, one frame scene, one irreversible step in every batch, and no bracket in sixty.** **The volume's goal is discharged and the page it discharges on is ch 778: she stops the room deciding by taking the light out of it herself, and the only thing that was still lit in that building goes out, and a boy of sixteen has to come up eight hundred and eighty steps to find out why.**

### D3, the bundle, in full, because it was a real regression and not a typo

**The count is five and it is now five everywhere.** Ch 749 records three insertions into the bundle of papers: **the seventh of the month beginning 2,324, the month beginning 2,354, and the third of the month beginning 2,414.** Ch 779 relisted the same three and **swapped the third for the month beginning 2,444 — a handling no page records — while dropping the one ch 749 does record.** Ch 779 then narrates two further handlings, on the second and the morning of the third of the month beginning 2,534, which takes it to five, and **ch 780 and ch 778 were both still saying three.**

- **`chapter-0779.md:27`** — the third date restored to **the third of the month beginning two thousand four hundred and fourteen**. The *three times* in that sentence is correct where it stands, because it is narrated before the second of the month.
- **`chapter-0780.md:117`** — **three times → five times.** This is the last page of the volume and she is reading out what is in that room, and by then she has had her arm in it five times.
- **`chapter-0778.md:61`** — **left at three times and it is right there**, because ch 778 is the first of the month beginning 2,534 and the two new handlings are on the second and the third, after it.
- **`state/continuity.md`** and **`state/current.md`** — both carried **four**, which matched nothing on the page, and both now carry five with the five dates named.

### D6, the one finding that did not reproduce

**The volume total for `in the ordinary voice` is 168 and the prompt was already right.** Measured on `grep -o "in the ordinary voice" chapters/volume-13/*.md | wc -l`: **56 in Batch 0001 · 79 in Batch 0002 · 15 in Batch 0003 · 18 in Batch 0004, summing to 168.** The reviewer’s 169 is one high and does not reproduce by this command or by the per-chapter counts. **It has not been adopted, and the prompt has been given the working so that the close cannot raise the total on a number that cannot be produced.** The same pass found that the neighbouring figure in this file — *`She said,` … the volume stands at 511* — matches nothing on the page and is **1,133** (251 · 371 · 285 · 226 by batch). That one was not in the findings and is corrected here, because the close was about to be handed a false total.

### D8, the echo kept and made deliberate

The two pairs were **ch 769 and ch 772**, which open the same way because ch 772 is ch 769's failure run again four days later and escalated, and **ch 778 and ch 779**, which open the same way because ch 779 is the same inventory read back in the dark. **Both echoes are the point of their chapters and neither was cut.** What was removed is the accident: the second of each pair now carries a clause that names the echo as the echo.

- **`chapter-0772.md:27`** — *She said it out loud on the flat of her back … and the whole of it came out in the same order it came out in last time, because there was nothing else in that room that would take it.*
- **`chapter-0779.md:85`** — *She said out loud, standing in the dark four feet off the near end of that table, in the same place she had stood in six days before.* **The six is checked: ch 778’s inventory is at the fourth hour of the first of the month beginning 2,534 and ch 779’s is at the seventh hour of the seventh, and the seventh is six days after the first.**
